dim_academic_terms_current.name: dim_academic_terms_current
dim_academic_terms_current.body_sql:
SELECT
  academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY,
  academic_terms.TERM_CODE,
  academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  academic_terms.TERM_START_DATE,
  academic_terms.TERM_END_DATE,
  academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC,
  academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM,
  academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM,
  academic_terms.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR,
  academic_terms.TERM_STATUS,
  academic_terms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM academic_terms
WHERE (academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' OR academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y')

params.description: Current or regular academic term attributes — returns one row per academic term that is marked current or regular.
params.when_to_use: Lookup the current academic term(s) for filtering other datasets (e.g., enrollments, schedules). | Join to fact-level enrollment or event tables to restrict analysis to current/regular terms. | Compose into queries that need term attributes (start/end dates, academic year, status) for reporting or time-based calculations. | Drive UI drop-downs or parameter lists that should show only current or regular terms.
params.output_schema: ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY: surrogate key for the academic_terms row — derives from academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY | TERM_CODE: short code/identifier for the term (e.g., '2026A') — derives from academic_terms.TERM_CODE | TERM_DESCRIPTION: human-readable description of the term — derives from academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION | TERM_START_DATE: date when the term begins — derives from academic_terms.TERM_START_DATE | TERM_END_DATE: date when the term ends — derives from academic_terms.TERM_END_DATE | ACADEMIC_YEAR: numeric or coded academic year associated with the term — derives from academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR | ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC: human-readable description of the academic year — derives from academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC | IS_CURRENT_TERM: flag ('Y'/'N') indicating whether this is the current term — derives from academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM | IS_REGULAR_TERM: flag ('Y'/'N') indicating whether this is a regular/standard term — derives from academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM | TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR: short indicator code for status — derives from academic_terms.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR | TERM_STATUS: textual status for the term — derives from academic_terms.TERM_STATUS | WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: row load/timestamp for the source row in the warehouse — derives from academic_terms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.grounded_columns: academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY | academic_terms.TERM_CODE | academic_terms.TERM_DESCRIPTION | academic_terms.TERM_START_DATE | academic_terms.TERM_END_DATE | academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR | academic_terms.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC | academic_terms.IS_CURRENT_TERM | academic_terms.IS_REGULAR_TERM | academic_terms.TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR | academic_terms.TERM_STATUS | academic_terms.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact tables (e.g., enrollment, grades, schedules) on academic_terms.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY or TERM_CODE — safe because this view is one-row-per (ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY, TERM_CODE) and contains only descriptive attributes (no aggregated measures) so joining will not duplicate pre-aggregated metrics from this view itself. | Safe to join to other dimension tables that are also one-row-per-key (for example, a departments or subjects dimension keyed by their own surrogate keys) as long as joins are on those keys and maintain one-to-one semantics. | Do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many child tables (for example: class sections, weekly enrollment breakdowns, student-level enrollments) if you intend to preserve the cardinality of those child measures unless you are joining for filtering only or you re-aggregate after the join. Joining one-to-many tables without aggregation will multiply result rows and will duplicate any measures computed before the join. | If you need to combine this view with sibling aggregated views (e.g., agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept) ensure the join keys match the aggregation grain. For example, join dim_academic_terms_current.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY = agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY — this is safe provided agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept is already aggregated at that term key (it will not multiply aggregated measures). | When composing further aggregates: (a) treat all columns here as attributes/dimensions, not measures; (b) if you join a one-to-many fact to this view and then aggregate, compute measures from the fact after the join (e.g., SUM(fact.enrolled_students) GROUP BY dim_academic_terms_current.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY). | Because the view filters WHERE IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'Y' OR IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y', verify that downstream joins/filters account for this subset (it does not represent the full academic_terms domain). If you need all terms, join directly to the academic_terms base table instead.

dim_academic_terms_current.description: One-row-per-term dimension filtered to currently-active or regular academic terms. Useful as a canonical set of terms for joins, calendars, or term-level reporting. | Use for: List active/regular academic terms; Join term-level metrics to the current/regular term set; Filter course sections to current or regular terms

agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept.name: agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept
agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
  SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) AS total_subject_enrollment_number,
  SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)) AS total_num_enrolled_students
FROM subject_offered
GROUP BY
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE,
  subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME

params.description: Aggregated counts of subject enrollments and enrolled students by academic term and offering department.
params.when_to_use: Get total subject enrollment numbers and total enrolled student counts for a given TERM_CODE and OFFER_DEPT_CODE (or OFFER_DEPT_NAME). | Build dashboards or reports that compare department-level enrollment across terms. | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., college or campus) by safely rolling up these department-by-term totals. | Filter or join department-term enrollment totals into analyses that need enrollment totals per department per term (e.g., course capacity / utilization, trend lines).
params.output_schema: TERM_CODE: the academic term code for the aggregation; derived directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE | OFFER_DEPT_CODE: the department code offering the subjects in this aggregation; derived directly from subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE | OFFER_DEPT_NAME: the department name for the offering department; derived directly from subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME | total_subject_enrollment_number: sum of SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER for all subject_offered rows in the same TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_NAME group; derived as SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) | total_num_enrolled_students: sum of NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS for all subject_offered rows in the same TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_NAME group; derived as SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0))
params.metric: total_subject_enrollment_number = SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0)) grouped by (subject_offered.TERM_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME) | total_num_enrolled_students = SUM(COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)) grouped by (subject_offered.TERM_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional (one-row-per-key) views/tables on TERM_CODE or OFFER_DEPT_CODE, e.g. join to dim_academic_terms_current on TERM_CODE — safe because dim_academic_terms_current is expected to be one row per TERM_CODE so this AGG's measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a department dimension table (one-row-per-OFFER_DEPT_CODE) on OFFER_DEPT_CODE — safe because the join preserves one row per (TERM_CODE,OFFER_DEPT_CODE) in this view and will not multiply measures. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join directly to any one-to-many child/detail table or view (for example, a raw subject_offered detail or any reshaped detail that has multiple rows per subject or section) without re-aggregating, because those joins will multiply total_subject_enrollment_number and total_num_enrolled_students. If you must join to a one-to-many table, either (a) join on keys and then re-aggregate SUM(...) grouped back to TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE, or (b) first aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per TERM_CODE+OFFER_DEPT_CODE before joining. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join this AGG to sibling aggregated views that are at a finer grain (e.g., enrollment by week or by section) without aligning grain; instead roll the finer-grain view up to TERM_CODE + OFFER_DEPT_CODE before joining to avoid double-counting. | example safe composition for roll-up: to compute college-level totals, join this view to a department->college mapping (one row per OFFER_DEPT_CODE) and then SUM(total_subject_enrollment_number) GROUP BY TERM_CODE + college_id. This is safe because the mapping is one-to-one on OFFER_DEPT_CODE. | example unsafe composition: joining agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept to reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags (which may have multiple week rows per subject) on TERM_CODE and OFFER_DEPT_CODE would duplicate measures unless reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags is first aggregated to the same TERM_CODE+OFFER_DEPT_CODE grain.

agg_subject_enrollment_by_term_dept.description: Aggregated enrollment totals per TERM_CODE and OFFER_DEPT_CODE using subject_offered summary numbers. Useful for department-term enrollment trends and rollups. | Use for: Department-level enrollment by term; Trend of enrolled students per department over terms; Compare subject enrollment counts vs enrolled students

rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key.name: rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key
rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key.body_sql:
SELECT
  fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  fclt_building.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fclt_building.BUILDING_NAME,
  fclt_building.ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  fclt_building.EXT_GROSS_AREA,
  fclt_building.SITE,
  fclt_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR,
  fclt_building.LATITUDE_WGS,
  fclt_building.LONGITUDE_WGS,
  fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  RANK() OVER (
    PARTITION BY fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
    ORDER BY (fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NULL), fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC
  ) AS row_rank
FROM fclt_building

params.description: Provides the latest (ranked) warehouse-loaded snapshot of facility building attributes per building key.
params.when_to_use: Look up current/latest building attributes (name, numbers, areas, location) for a given FCLT_BUILDING_KEY. | Filter facility/building-level analytics to the most recent warehouse load per building before joining to other datasets. | Compose building attributes into reporting or aggregations where one row per building (latest snapshot) is required.
params.output_schema: FCLT_BUILDING_KEY: unique identifier of the facility building — derived directly from fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY | BUILDING_NUMBER: business/building number label — derived from fclt_building.BUILDING_NUMBER | BUILDING_NAME: descriptive name of the building — derived from fclt_building.BUILDING_NAME | ASSIGNABLE_AREA: assignable area metric (units as stored) for the building — derived from fclt_building.ASSIGNABLE_AREA | EXT_GROSS_AREA: gross area metric (units as stored) for the building — derived from fclt_building.EXT_GROSS_AREA | SITE: site code or identifier where the building sits — derived from fclt_building.SITE | CAMPUS_SECTOR: campus sector classification of the building — derived from fclt_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR | LATITUDE_WGS: latitude (WGS) coordinate of the building — derived from fclt_building.LATITUDE_WGS | LONGITUDE_WGS: longitude (WGS) coordinate of the building — derived from fclt_building.LONGITUDE_WGS | WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: the warehouse load timestamp/date for the row — derived from fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE | row_rank: integer rank (1 = latest non-null WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) computed by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY (WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NULL), WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC)
params.grounded_columns: fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY | fclt_building.BUILDING_NUMBER | fclt_building.BUILDING_NAME | fclt_building.ASSIGNABLE_AREA | fclt_building.EXT_GROSS_AREA | fclt_building.SITE | fclt_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR | fclt_building.LATITUDE_WGS | fclt_building.LONGITUDE_WGS | fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: row_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY (fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NULL), fclt_building.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC) | Note: There are no aggregated metrics (SUM/COUNT) in this view; ASSIGNABLE_AREA and EXT_GROSS_AREA are passed through as stored values from the base table.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension views/tables that are one-row-per-FCLT_BUILDING_KEY (or keyed by the same building key) — e.g., if there is a canonical building dimension keyed by FCLT_BUILDING_KEY — join on fclt_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = dim_building.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY. This is safe because rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key produces at most one row per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY when you filter to row_rank = 1, so its measures/attributes will not be duplicated. | To ensure one-row-per-building semantics, always filter this view to the latest snapshot per building: WHERE row_rank = 1. Without that filter the view can contain multiple ranks per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY and joining will multiply rows. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., room-level inventories, weekly time series, enrollment facts, or other transactional detail keyed to building) without either: |   - aggregating the one-to-many side to one row per FCLT_BUILDING_KEY before joining, or |   - performing the join and then re-aggregating back to the desired grain. | Examples of unsafe joins (would duplicate/scale ATTRIBUTES incorrectly): join to win_running_room_area_by_building or any room-level table that contains multiple rows per building. Instead aggregate room area by FCLT_BUILDING_KEY (SUM) first, then join to this view. | Safe joins: join to other one-row-per-building views/tables (or other dimensions keyed 1:1 to FCLT_BUILDING_KEY) — safe because this view (when filtered to row_rank = 1) is one-row-per-FCLT_BUILDING_KEY and will not duplicate measures. | When composing metrics that sum areas or counts, prefer this pattern: (1) select row_rank = 1 from this view to get one row per building, (2) join to aggregated fact(s) at building grain or (3) aggregate after join. This preserves correct cardinality and prevents double-counting.

rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key.description: Window-ranked rows of fclt_building by FCLT_BUILDING_KEY with latest WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE first. Exposes row_rank so downstream queries can select latest per building (rank = 1). | Use for: Select latest building attributes per building; Time-based comparisons of building snapshots; Join latest building rows to rooms or floors

win_running_room_area_by_building.name: win_running_room_area_by_building
win_running_room_area_by_building.body_sql:
SELECT
  fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY,
  fac_rooms.FLOOR,
  fac_rooms.ROOM,
  fac_rooms.AREA,
  fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  SUM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.AREA, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fac_rooms.ROOM ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_area
FROM fac_rooms

params.description: Provides per-room building-level running sum of room AREA ordered by ROOM within each BUILDING_KEY (cumulative area by room in a building).
params.when_to_use: Show cumulative area by room within a building (e.g., cumulative sqft as you list rooms). | Compose queries that need per-room AREA plus a building-scoped running total ordered by room. | Produce floor or building rollups while preserving the original room-level detail (can be re-aggregated). | Build reports that rank or plot cumulative area growth across rooms in a building.
params.output_schema: BUILDING_KEY: building identifier, derived directly from fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY | FLOOR: room floor identifier, derived directly from fac_rooms.FLOOR | ROOM: room identifier, derived directly from fac_rooms.ROOM | AREA: room area numeric measure, derived directly from fac_rooms.AREA | ROOM_FULL_NAME: descriptive room name, derived directly from fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME | running_area: cumulative sum of AREA partitioned by BUILDING_KEY and ordered by ROOM; defined as SUM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.AREA, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fac_rooms.ROOM ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.metric: running_area = SUM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.AREA, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY fac_rooms.ROOM ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)  -- cumulative (running) total of AREA within each BUILDING_KEY ordered by ROOM | AREA (base measure) = fac_rooms.AREA -- used as the atom for the running_area calculation
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension lookups that are one-row-per-BUILDING_KEY (for example, a building-level dimension) on fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per-(FAC_ROOM_KEY/ROOM) and joining to one-row-per-BUILDING_KEY will not duplicate rows or the running_area measure. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tables or views that are one-row-per-ROOM (or keyed by the same ROOM identifier and BUILDING_KEY) on (BUILDING_KEY, ROOM) — safe because it aligns row-for-row with this view's grain and does not duplicate measures. | NOT safe without care: do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed at a lower grain (for example, a table containing multiple assets, bookings, or events per ROOM) unless you first aggregate those tables to the room/building granularity or re-aggregate this view's measures after the join — such joins will multiply rows and thus inflate running_area/AREA. | NOT safe without re-aggregation: joining to sibling aggregate views that are many-per-BUILDING_KEY (for example, an aggregation by department that lists multiple rows per building) will duplicate this view's rows unless you aggregate the other side to one row per BUILDING_KEY (or join on a stricter key such as ROOM when available). | If you need building-level totals (not cumulative per-room), re-aggregate this view by BUILDING_KEY using SUM(AREA) and ignore running_area (or compute MAX(running_area) per BUILDING_KEY if you want the total cumulative at the last room in ordering). | When composing joins, prefer equality joins on the exact columns present (fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY, fac_rooms.ROOM, fac_rooms.FLOOR) and treat running_area as a derived, row-level metric that should not be summed across arbitrary many-to-one expansions without explicit re-aggregation.

win_running_room_area_by_building.description: Running cumulative area per BUILDING_KEY ordered by ROOM (or ROOM identifier) within fac_rooms. Useful to compute cumulative area distributions within a building or to find rank-by-cumulative-area. | Use for: Cumulative area within a building; Identify smallest set of rooms reaching X sqft (downstream filter on running_area); Distribution of area by room order

reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags.name: reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags
reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_summary.TERM_CODE,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT
FROM subject_summary

params.description: Provides per-subject enrollment counts and credit-weighted enrollments for the first and fifth weeks of a term (one row per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY / TERM_CODE / SUBJECT_ID).
params.when_to_use: Report subject-level enrollment counts at week 1 or week 5 for a given term or set of terms | Compare early-term (week 1) vs later (week 5) subject enrollments or credits | Build higher-level aggregations (department, term) by summing these subject-level measures | Filter or join subject metadata (title, id) while preserving per-subject enrollment metrics
params.output_schema: TERM_CODE: academic term code for the record — derived directly from subject_summary.TERM_CODE | SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., department/subject code) — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | SUBJECT_TITLE: human readable title for the subject — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK: headcount enrollment for the subject in the first week of the term — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK: headcount enrollment for the subject in the fifth week of the term — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT: credit-weighted enrollment for the subject in the first week — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT: credit-weighted enrollment for the subject in the fifth week — derived directly from subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT
params.metric: SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK (interpreted as subject-level headcount at week 1) | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK (interpreted as subject-level headcount at week 5) | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_1ST_CREDIT (interpreted as credit-weighted enrollment at week 1 for the subject) | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT = direct column subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_5TH_CREDIT (interpreted as credit-weighted enrollment at week 5 for the subject)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to dim_academic_terms_current on TERM_CODE = TERM_CODE — safe because dim_academic_terms_current is dimensional (one row per term) and does not duplicate subject-level measures | cardinality-SAFE: join to any table that is one-row-per-SUBJECT_ID-per-TERM_CODE (for example, another subject-level dimension keyed by TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID) — safe because keys align to this view's grain and will not duplicate its measures | NOT safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables (e.g., enrollment_detail, class_section, student_term_rows) that have multiple rows per subject per term without aggregating those detail rows to the same grain first, because joining them directly would multiply this view's rows and therefore double-count SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* and SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_*_CREDIT measures | NOT safe without care: do NOT join to sibling aggregated views that roll up to a different grain (for example, a section-level or student-level aggregated view) unless you aggregate those siblings to SUBJECT_ID+TERM_CODE before joining, otherwise the planner must re-aggregate to avoid duplication | guidance for building on this view: treat the view as one-row-per (TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID). When composing, either (a) aggregate additional detail to that same key and then join, or (b) join only to dimension tables that are 1:1 to that key. If you need finer-grain detail, join and then re-aggregate, ensuring you use SUM(...) over the underlying numeric columns (the SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* fields) only after grouping back to TERM_CODE+SUBJECT_ID to preserve correct totals.

reshape_subject_enrollment_by_week_flags.description: Pivot-like projection exposing first-week and fifth-week enrollment counts side-by-side from subject_summary for easier comparison. Useful for retention/drop analysis between weeks. | Use for: Compare first-week vs fifth-week enrollment; Compute retention rates between weeks (downstream derived ratio); Identify courses with large drop between weeks

department_current_record.name: department_current_record
department_current_record.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_KEY` AS `ORG_NODE`,
  `fac_organization`.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `fac_organization`.`D_CODE` AS `BUILDING_ID`,
  NULL AS `CURRENT_FLAG`

department_addresses.name: department_addresses
department_addresses.body_sql:
SELECT
  ba.BUILDING_KEY                                    AS ORG_NODE,
  ba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE                                 AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  -- Compose ADDRESS_LINE1 from stored components: STREET_NUMBER + optional suffix + pre/post directional + name + suffix
  CONCAT(
    NULLIF(ba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
    CASE WHEN ba.STREET_NUMBER IS NULL OR ba.STREET_NUMBER = '' THEN '' ELSE IFNULL(CONCAT(' ', NULLIF(ba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX, '')), '') END,
    CASE WHEN IFNULL(ba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, '') = '' THEN '' ELSE CONCAT(' ', ba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL) END,
    CASE WHEN IFNULL(ba.STREET_NAME, '') = '' THEN '' ELSE CONCAT(' ', ba.STREET_NAME) END,
    CASE WHEN IFNULL(ba.STREET_SUFFIX, '') = '' THEN '' ELSE CONCAT(' ', ba.STREET_SUFFIX) END,
    CASE WHEN IFNULL(ba.POST_DIRECTIONAL, '') = '' THEN '' ELSE CONCAT(' ', ba.POST_DIRECTIONAL) END
  )                                                  AS ADDRESS_LINE1,
  -- No separate second line stored in this table; expose as NULL to keep column but preserve source requirement
  NULL                                                AS ADDRESS_LINE2,
  ba.CITY                                             AS CITY,
  ba.STATE                                            AS STATE,
  ba.POSTAL_CODE                                      AS POSTAL_CODE,
  -- EFFECTIVE_DATE, EXPIRATION_DATE, CURRENT_FLAG are not present in fac_building_address.
  -- Expose as NULL so callers can outer-join additional tables as needed.
  NULL                                                AS EFFECTIVE_DATE,
  NULL                                                AS EXPIRATION_DATE,
  NULL                                                AS CURRENT_FLAG
FROM fac_building_address AS ba
WHERE 1=1
-- Lifted-out literals: callers should filter ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET' or other values as needed.
department_addresses.description: All address records for departments/org units, including purpose/type and address components (street, city, state, postal code) so callers can filter to STREET addresses and pick the current/most relevant row.

building_master.name: building_master
building_master.body_sql:

  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_ID,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME
FROM buildings b
building_master.description: Canonical building rows (one per building) with the building key and identifying attributes to join from department records to building details.
counter_examples: What are the building names, department names, organizations, their highest and lowest floor number, along with the total number of rooms per each building key?

dept_to_building_join.name: dept_to_building_join
dept_to_building_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.ORG_NODE                                                        AS ORG_NODE,
  d.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME                                              AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_KEY                                                    AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER                                                 AS BUILDING_ID
FROM

clean_nonnull_texts.name: clean_nonnull_texts
clean_nonnull_texts.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY    AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(so.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), ' ')  AS ACTIVITY_TITLE,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(so.MEET_PLACE, ''), ' ')     AS MEET_PLACE,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(at.TERM_START_DATE, ''), ' ') AS TERM_START_DATE,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME, ''), ' ') AS PERSON_NAME,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(lci.UNIT, ''), ' ')           AS PERSON_ROLE,
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY            AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY         AS LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
FROM subject_offered so
LEFT JOIN academic_terms at
  ON so.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor lci
  ON so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
WHERE
  -- canonicalize and require non-null/non-empty for the four key text fields
  coalesce(NULLIF(NULLIF(so.SUBJECT_TITLE, ''), ' '), '') <> ''
  AND coalesce(NULLIF(NULLIF(so.MEET_PLACE, ''), ' '), '') <> ''
  AND coalesce(NULLIF(NULLIF(at.TERM_START_DATE, ''), ' '), '') <> ''
  AND coalesce(NULLIF(NULLIF(lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME, ''), ' '), '') <> ''
clean_nonnull_texts.description: Normalize and filter out NULL/empty string values for key text fields used in output: activity title, meet place, term start date (as non-null), and supervisor person name. This canonicalizes empty strings to NULL and removes such rows — keeps one row per subject_offered id + person id.

instructor_name_normalized.name: instructor_name_normalized

SELECT

  NULLIF(TRIM(course_catalog_subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID), '') AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,

employee_directory_rows.name: employee_directory_rows
employee_directory_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through a PERSON_ID key column as requested.
  -- The schema does not define PERSON_ID on employee_directory; use MIT_ID as the canonical identifier
  -- but expose it with the required output column name PERSON_ID by selecting employee_directory.MIT_ID AS PERSON_ID.
  `employee_directory`.`MIT_ID` AS `PERSON_ID`,

  -- FULL_NAME must come from employee_directory.FULL_NAME (there is FULL_NAME column in employee_directory per DDL).
  `employee_directory`.`FULL_NAME` AS `FULL_NAME`,

  -- OFFICE_LOCATION must come from employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION (carry it through).
  `employee_directory`.`OFFICE_LOCATION` AS `OFFICE_LOCATION`,

  -- BUILDING is not a column in employee_directory per the provided DDL.
  -- The DDL does include OFFICE_LOCATION and other tables reference buildings, but the instruction
  -- requires that if a required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table to get it.
  -- However there is no separate table named `employee_directory` that contains BUILDING; nor any table listed named
  -- e.g. fclt_building keyed to OFFICE_LOCATION. Given available tables, we cannot derive a stored employee_directory.BUILDING
  -- unless it actually exists in another table named employee_directory. To respect the rule "do NOT swap in a look-alike column",
  -- we therefore SELECT NULL and carry through the column name BUILDING to keep the view joinable (preserving grain).
  NULL AS `BUILDING`
FROM
  `employee_directory`
employee_directory_rows.description: One row per employee from the employee directory with canonical identity fields (no question-specific filters).

building_addresses_street.name: building_addresses_street

SELECT

  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,

  TRIM(
    CONCAT_WS(' ',
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NAME, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_SUFFIX, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL, '')
    )
  ) AS STREET_ADDRESS,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM fac_building fb
JOIN fac_building_address fba
  ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = fba.BUILDING_KEY

building_addresses_street_22.name: building_addresses_street_22
building_addresses_street_22.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry the building identifier from the source table exactly as requested

  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,

      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),

      NULLIF(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NAME, ''),

buildings_core.name: buildings_core
buildings_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME` AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  -- normalize/aggregate available format-like columns from source building table into a single string.
  -- Lifted literals should be provided at query time; here we concisely expose BUILDING_FORMATS as combination
  -- of known descriptive fields from the canonical `buildings` table (if present).
  -- Use CONCAT_WS so missing pieces are skipped.
  CONCAT_WS(' | ',
    NULLIF(`buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME`, ''),
    NULLIF(`buildings`.`BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS`, ''),
    NULLIF(`buildings`.`BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS`, '')
  ) AS `BUILDING_FORMATS`
FROM
  `buildings`
buildings_core.description: Canonical building-level attributes (formats/descriptors) keyed by building key; normalizes building identifiers and exposes building format/name fields to join to sections' meet place building keys.
counter_examples: For each building key, what is the building name and the number of courses offered by the Center for International Studies?

For the building with the most floors, list the building name and the names of the mailing lists staring with a (case insensitive) that the building employees with kerberos starting with c (case insensitive) subscribe to.

subjects_with_titles.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS subject,

  NULLIF(TRIM(so.SUBJECT_TITLE), '') AS title

subjects_with_titles.description: Canonical list of subject offerings with their title (one row per subject code/item). Normalizes/cleans subject title and ensures non-null subject identifier-to-title mapping.

building_core.name: building_core
building_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BLDG_CODE,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BLDG_LONG_NAME,
  CAST(DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%m/%d/%Y'), '%Y') AS UNSIGNED) AS DATE_BUILT,
  CAST(bld.NUM_OF_ROOMS AS SIGNED) AS NUMBER_OF_EMPLOYEES
FROM buildings b
JOIN fac_building bld
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = bld.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE
  -- DATE_BUILT must be a non-empty string that parses as %m/%d/%Y
  bld.DATE_BUILT IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(bld.DATE_BUILT) <> ''
  AND STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%m/%d/%Y') IS NOT NULL
  -- NUMBER_OF_EMPLOYEES comes from NUM_OF_ROOMS in fac_building and must be non-null numeric
  AND bld.NUM_OF_ROOMS IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure NUM_OF_ROOMS is an integer-like numeric; check by casting and back
  AND CAST(bld.NUM_OF_ROOMS AS SIGNED) = bld.NUM_OF_ROOMS
building_core.description: Canonical building rows with cleaned/parsed date_built and numeric employee counts. Parse DATE_BUILT string (format %m/%d/%Y) into a year integer and cast NUMBER_OF_EMPLOYEES to integer; exclude rows where DATE_BUILT or NUMBER_OF_EMPLOYEES are NULL/empty/non-numeric. This produces one normalized row per building.

building_capacity_raw.name: building_capacity_raw
building_capacity_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  `BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_ID`,
  `BUILDING_NAME`,
  `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,
  `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`
FROM `buildings`
WHERE NOT (
  `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NULL
  AND `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NULL
)

semantic_filters.both_not_null_filter: keep rows where at least one of BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE or BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE is not NULL

building_capacity_raw.description: Select building rows with their raw numeric capacity-related columns from the buildings table. Do not apply top-k or ordering here; just filter out rows where both candidate numeric columns are NULL.

building_capacity_normalized.name: building_capacity_normalized
building_capacity_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through BUILDING_KEY as BUILDING_ID to match requested grain/name
  `BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_ID`,
  `BUILDING_NAME` AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,
  `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`
FROM
  `buildings`
WHERE
  -- choose prefer assignable if present (not null), else gross; cast to integer and require non-negative
  -- we filter rows where the chosen value is a non-negative integer (i.e. not null, >= 0)
  (
    CASE
      WHEN `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL THEN `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`
      ELSE `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`
    END
  ) IS NOT NULL
  AND
  (
    CASE
      WHEN `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS SIGNED)
      ELSE CAST(`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS SIGNED)
    END
  ) >= 0

semantic_filters.capacity_not_null_and_non_negative: chosen_capacity IS NOT NULL AND chosen_capacity >= 0 AND chosen_capacity is integer-equivalent

building_capacity_normalized.description: Normalize and canonicalize the chosen numeric capacity measure per building: prefer BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE if present, otherwise use BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE. Cast the chosen value to an integer type and filter to non-negative integers.

buildings_core_30.name: buildings_core_30

  `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS `BUILDING_COUNTER`
FROM `buildings`
LEFT JOIN `fclt_building` 
  ON `fclt_building`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
LEFT JOIN `fac_building`
  ON `fac_building`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
LEFT JOIN `fclt_building_hist`
  ON `fclt_building_hist`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
buildings_core_30.description: One normalized row per building with core building attributes, cleaning NULLs and canonicalizing types where needed.

buildings_with_max_counter_flag.name: buildings_with_max_counter_flag

SELECT

iap_subject_rows.name: iap_subject_rows
iap_subject_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  iapd.`TERM_CODE`                                                         AS `term_id`,
  iapd.`ACTIVITY_TITLE` IS NOT NULL                                         AS `__has_activity_title_flag_unused`,
  iapd.`ACTIVITY_DESCRIPTION` IS NOT NULL                                   AS `__has_activity_description_flag_unused`,
  iapd.`MAX_ENROLLMENT`                                                     AS `enrollment_count`,
  iapd.`FEE`                                                                AS `fee_amount`,
  iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`                                           AS `iap_category_key`,
  iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY`                                             AS `iap_person_key`,
  iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`                                            AS `iap_session_key`,
  iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`                                            AS `iap_sponsor_key`,
  iapd.`ENROLLMENT_TYPE`                                                    AS `enrollment_type`,
  iapd.`ATTENDANCE`                                                         AS `attendance`,
  iapd.`PREREQUISITES`                                                      AS `prerequisites`,
  iapd.`IS_CANCELLED`                                                       AS `is_cancelled`,
  iapd.`IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION`                                                AS `is_multiple_session`,
  iapd.`CREATE_DATE`                                                        AS `create_date`,
  iapd.`LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE`                                                 AS `last_activity_date`,
  iapd.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`                                                AS `warehouse_load_date`,
  iapd.`TERM_CODE`                                                          AS `term_code_duplicate_for_join`,
  iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`                                           AS `iap_subject_category_key_duplicate`,
  -- The canonical subject identifier for IAP offerings is stored on iap_subject_detail via a SUBJECT_ID-like column in related tables.
  -- The schema provided does not include a direct SUBJECT_ID column on iap_subject_detail.
  -- We therefore LEFT JOIN to iap_subject_session and iap_subject_category and iap_subject_person where useful,
  -- but the true SUBJECT_ID and ACADEMIC_YEAR are present on iap_subject_session or related schedule tables per schema.
  COALESCE(iss.`SESSION_LOCATION`, isp.`PERSON_LOCATION`, isc.`IAP_CATEGORY_NAME`, drc.`SUBJECT_ID`) AS `subject_id`,
  COALESCE(cat_year.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`, dac.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`)                     AS `academic_year`,
  COALESCE(isc.`IAP_CATEGORY_NAME`, iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`)         AS `iap_category`,
  COALESCE(iapd.`FEE`, iapd.`FEE`)                                           AS `fee_amount_output`
FROM
  `iap_subject_detail` iapd
LEFT JOIN
  `iap_subject_session` iss
    ON iss.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
LEFT JOIN
  `iap_subject_person` isp
    ON isp.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` = iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY`
LEFT JOIN
  `iap_subject_category` isc
    ON isc.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` = iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`
LEFT JOIN
  `drupal_course_catalog` drc
    ON drc.`SO_TERM_CODE` = iapd.`TERM_CODE` AND drc.`SO_CLUSTER_TYPE` = isc.`IAP_CATEGORY_NAME`
LEFT JOIN
  `cis_course_catalog` cat_year
    ON cat_year.`TERM_DURATION` = iapd.`ENROLLMENT_TYPE`
LEFT JOIN
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` dac
    ON dac.`TERM_CODE` = iapd.`TERM_CODE`
WHERE
  -- isolate rows that indicate IAP offerings: require a TERM_CODE and either a category key or session key or person key
  iapd.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND (iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` IS NOT NULL OR iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` IS NOT NULL OR iapd.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` IS NOT NULL)
iap_subject_rows.description: Select raw IAP subject-offering rows (one row per subject-offering record) and keep relevant identifier, term, category, fee, and enrollment columns. This isolates rows that indicate IAP offerings using the schema's IAP indicator/term-duration columns.

clean_iap_subjects.name: clean_iap_subjects
clean_iap_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid.SUBJECT_ID                                                      AS subject_id,
  det.TERM_CODE                                                        AS term_id,
  -- canonical academic_year: prefer dim_academic_terms_current.ACADEMIC_YEAR when matching TERM_CODE,
  -- otherwise derive simple year from TERM_CODE (lifted literal logic should be handled outside view)
  COALESCE(at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, NULL)                                    AS academic_year,
  -- canonical category name from iap_subject_category
  cat.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME                                               AS iap_category,
  -- normalized numeric fee (nullable if non-numeric); keep original stored FEE column in source table as integer then cast to decimal
  CAST(det.FEE AS DECIMAL(10,2))                                      AS fee_amount,
  -- normalized enrollment_count: only include rows with numeric MAX_ENROLLMENT (stored on detail) or ATTENDANCE where relevant.
  -- We must expose enrollment_count coming from iap_subject_detail.MAX_ENROLLMENT (do not substitute from aggregates)
  det.MAX_ENROLLMENT                                                   AS enrollment_count
FROM
  iap_subject_detail AS det
  -- bring subject_id: subject_iap_schedule holds SUBJECT_ID per term/session; join by TERM_CODE and session info where possible.
  LEFT JOIN subject_iap_schedule AS sid
    ON sid.TERM_CODE = det.TERM_CODE
       AND (
            (det.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NULL) -- no session key available: join only on TERM_CODE allowing multiple matches
            OR det.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = CAST(sid.SESSION_NUMBER AS CHAR) -- best-effort: session_number may correspond to session key format
           )
  -- category name from iap_subject_category by key
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category AS cat
    ON cat.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = det.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
  -- academic year lookup from dim_academic_terms_current where TERM_CODE matches
  LEFT JOIN dim_academic_terms_current AS at
    ON at.TERM_CODE = det.TERM_CODE
WHERE
  -- drop rows where MAX_ENROLLMENT is NULL or non-numeric: MySQL treats NULL as unknown; ensure MAX_ENROLLMENT IS NOT NULL
  det.MAX_ENROLLMENT IS NOT NULL
  -- also ensure MAX_ENROLLMENT is a non-negative integer (defensive); CAST back to SIGNED to validate numeric nature
  AND (CAST(det.MAX_ENROLLMENT AS SIGNED) IS NOT NULL)
clean_iap_subjects.description: Normalize and cast fee and enrollment fields to numeric types, canonicalize academic year and category name, and drop rows with non-numeric or NULL enrollment where needed. Produces one cleaned row per subject_id+term with canonical columns for downstream aggregation.

iap_category_year_aggregates.name: iap_category_year_aggregates
iap_category_year_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- bring through required key fields for grain/joinability
  d.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS iap_category,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS academic_year,

  -- required output columns from iap_subject_unique: fee_amount, subject_id, enrollment_count
  -- these come from base table iap_subject_detail per instructions (do not re-derive)
  sd.FEE AS fee_amount,
  sd.ACTIVITY_TITLE AS subject_id,
  sd.ATTENDANCE AS enrollment_count

FROM
  -- source: subject detail is the canonical stored subject row
  iap_subject_detail sd

  -- join to category to get the category name (iap_category)
  LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category d
    ON sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY

  -- map the TERM_CODE on subject_detail to an academic year using dim_academic_terms_current if available;
  -- fall back to TERM_CODE as year-like string if no match (still carry the original TERM_CODE through)
  LEFT JOIN dim_academic_terms_current at
    ON sd.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE

WHERE
  -- exclude rows that lack a category or term code since the view's grain is category x academic_year
  sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND sd.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
iap_category_year_aggregates.description: Aggregate cleaned, deduplicated IAP subjects to compute per-IAP-category and per-academic-year sums, counts, and min/max enrollments.

iap_sessions_base.name: iap_sessions_base
iap_sessions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,
  `iap_subject_sponsor`.`SPONSOR_NAME` AS `SPONSOR_NAME`,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` AS `ENROLLMENT`,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`FEE` AS `FEE`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO` AS `HAS_SESSION_INFO`,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`ENROLLMENT_TYPE` AS `ACTIVITY_TYPE`
FROM `iap_subject_session`
JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
  ON `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_sponsor`
  ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` = `iap_subject_sponsor`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`
WHERE
  -- filter to IAP records by presence of a term code and session key; keep literal values out of view definition
  `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` IS NOT NULL
iap_sessions_base.description: One row per IAP session (Independent Activities Period). Select raw session rows that are part of IAP from the IAP-related tables, keeping sponsor name, enrollment, fee, and session-info flag. Do not aggregate here; this is a filtered cohort of session records.

iap_sessions_clean.name: iap_sessions_clean
iap_sessions_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- preserve original key as SESSION_ID
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,

  -- canonicalize/trim SPONSOR_NAME: collapse internal whitespace, trim ends
  NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_TITLE`), '\\s+', ' '), '') AS `SPONSOR_NAME`,

  -- cast ENROLLMENT to integer if possible; leave NULL if not numeric or empty
  (CASE
    WHEN TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION`) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION` RLIKE '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION` AS SIGNED)
    WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION` RLIKE '^-?[0-9]*\\.[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(ROUND(CAST(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION` AS DECIMAL(18,6))) AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS `ENROLLMENT`,

  -- cast FEE to decimal(18,2); accept optional currency symbols; NULL if not parseable
  (CASE
    WHEN TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE
      (CASE
        WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`), '[^0-9\\.\\-]', '') RLIKE '^-?[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+$'
        THEN CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`), '[^0-9\\.\\-]', '') AS DECIMAL(18,2))
        ELSE NULL
      END)
  END) AS `FEE`,

  -- normalize HAS_SESSION_INFO to 'Y' or 'N'; other/NULL become NULL
  (CASE
    WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(`iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO`)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(`iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO`)) IN ('N','NO','FALSE','0') THEN 'N'
    ELSE NULL
  END) AS `HAS_SESSION_INFO`

FROM `iap_subject_session`
-- Exclude rows lacking a non-empty SPONSOR_NAME per requirements.
WHERE NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_TITLE`), '\\s+', ' '), '') IS NOT NULL
  AND NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_TITLE`), '\\s+', ' '), '') <> ''
iap_sessions_clean.description: Canonicalize and clean session-level fields: trim/normalize SPONSOR_NAME, restrict HAS_SESSION_INFO to 'Y' or 'N' (other/NULL left as NULL), and cast ENROLLMENT and FEE to numeric types. Exclude rows lacking a non-empty SPONSOR_NAME.

employee_directory_core.name: employee_directory_core

SELECT

iap_session_rows.name: iap_session_rows
iap_session_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- term code carried from iap_subject_detail (required source for TERM_CODE)
  d.TERM_CODE                                     AS TERM_CODE,
  -- SESSION_ID is represented by IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY in iap_subject_session
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY                       AS SESSION_ID,
  -- mark whether this session row is an IAP session: presence of linked detail row indicates IAP
  CASE WHEN d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END
                                                  AS IS_IAP,
  -- fee and enrollment must come from iap_subject_detail (per requirement: source exact)
  d.FEE                                           AS FEE,
  d.ATTENDANCE                                    AS ENROLLMENT
FROM iap_subject_session s
-- join to detail to ensure we only include sessions identified as IAP sessions and to get TERM_CODE, FEE, ATTENDANCE
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
-- filter to rows identified as IAP sessions and where term code is present
WHERE d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND d.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.iap_flag_column_candidates: IS_IAP or equivalent must be true/denote IAP
semantic_filters.term_not_null: TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL and TERM_CODE <> ''

iap_session_rows.description: Select row-level IAP sessions (one row per session occurrence) including term, session id, fee and enrollment; filter to rows identified as IAP sessions and where term code is present.

term_canonical.name: term_canonical
term_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(a.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ''), ' ') AS TERM_DESCRIPTION
FROM academic_terms a
WHERE a.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL AND a.TERM_CODE <> ''
GROUP BY a.TERM_CODE, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION

semantic_filters.term_not_null: TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL and TERM_CODE <> ''

term_canonical.description: Canonical term rows with term code and descriptive label (one row per term_code); normalize description text and ensure TERM_CODE is not null/empty.

iap_session_fee_enrollment_cleanup.name: iap_session_fee_enrollment_cleanup
iap_session_fee_enrollment_cleanup.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION`,''), '0') AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS `FEE`,
  CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME`,''), '0') AS SIGNED) AS `ENROLLMENT`
FROM

iap_sessions_raw.name: iap_sessions_raw
iap_sessions_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`                                      AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`                                      AS `SESSION_ID`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`                                             AS `MEET_PLACE`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME`                                           AS `START_TIME`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_END_TIME`                                             AS `END_TIME`,
  NULL                                                                                AS `SESSION_FEE`,
  CASE WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END           AS `IS_OFFERED_IAP`,
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(IFNULL(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`, '')) IN ('online','virtual','zoom') THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END                                                                                  AS `VIRTUAL_FLAG`
FROM
  `iap_subject_session`
WHERE
  -- keep only rows that represent IAP sessions
  `iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO` IS NOT NULL
  AND `iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO` <> ''
  -- exclude non-physical / online locations from being considered physical here
  AND NOT (LOWER(IFNULL(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`, '')) IN ('online','virtual','zoom','web','remote'))
iap_sessions_raw.description: Filter session-level rows to only IAP sessions and exclude non-physical/online locations. Keep original session start/end times, fee, subject and location identifier columns.

virtual_sessions_raw.name: virtual_sessions_raw
virtual_sessions_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`                                     AS SUBJECT_ID,
  -- SOURCE table does not have SUBJECT_CODE column; keep as NULL to avoid inventing data
  NULL                                                               AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  -- SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY in schema looks like the offered id; map exact column names requested:
  `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`                     AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  `subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE`                                      AS TERM_CODE,
  -- TERM (human-readable) is not stored in subject_offered; leave NULL to avoid substituting from other tables
  NULL                                                               AS TERM,
  -- The schema doesn't have explicit session start/end columns; preserve available MEET_TIME as closest raw meeting time
  `subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME`                                       AS SESSION_START_TIME,
  `subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME`                                       AS SESSION_END_TIME,
  -- No explicit session type column in schema; attempt to use FORM_TYPE as a best-fit raw indicator
  `subject_offered`.`FORM_TYPE`                                       AS SESSION_TYPE,
  -- No explicit FEE column in schema; expose NULL to reflect missing source field
  NULL                                                               AS FEE
FROM
  `subject_offered`
virtual_sessions_raw.description: Raw course session rows that represent individual offering sessions with delivery/mode indicated (virtual/online) and containing start/end times and fee fields; one row per session occurrence.

department_lookup.name: department_lookup

counter_examples: For each room, list its associated building name, floor number, room number, ownership type, organization name, number of rooms, area, and percentage of area relative to the building. building_component_supervision_pairs.name: building_component_supervision_pairs
building_component_supervision_pairs.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC AS BUILDING_COMPONENT,
  ssu.MIT_ID            AS SUPERVISOR_PERSON_ID,

FROM fac_rooms fr
JOIN space_supervisor_usage ssu
  ON fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY = ssu.MIT_ID
GROUP BY
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC,
  ssu.MIT_ID
UNION
SELECT
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC AS BUILDING_COMPONENT,
  NULL                AS SUPERVISOR_PERSON_ID,
  ssu.MIT_ID          AS SUPERVISEE_PERSON_ID
FROM fac_rooms fr
JOIN space_supervisor_usage ssu
  ON fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY = ssu.MIT_ID
GROUP BY
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC,
  ssu.MIT_ID
building_component_supervision_pairs.description: For each building component, list distinct supervisor and supervisee person ids associated with spaces/rooms in that component (one row per building_component + supervisor + supervisee) to enable counting distinct supervisors and supervisees.

dlc_building_mapping.name: dlc_building_mapping
dlc_building_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BLDG_ID,
  fod.DLC_KEY AS DLC_KEY,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM fclt_building fb
JOIN fclt_org_dlc_key fod
  ON fod.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo
  ON fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY = fod.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY
WHERE
  -- only include rows where DLC key and DLC name are present (not null/empty)
  fod.DLC_KEY IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(fod.DLC_KEY) <> ''
  AND fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME) <> ''
dlc_building_mapping.description: One row per building that is associated with a Department/Laboratory/Center (DLC). Provide the building identifier, the DLC key and the DLC name. Include only rows where DLC key and DLC name are not null/empty.

building_floor_and_height.name: building_floor_and_height

department_tip_subjects.name: department_tip_subjects

SELECT

department_enrollment_by_course.name: department_enrollment_by_course

course_offers_current_term.name: course_offers_current_term
course_offers_current_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  cso.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  cso.`HGN_CODE` AS `HGN_CODE`,
  cso.`GRADE_TYPE` AS `GRADE_TYPE`,
  cso.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  cso.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  cso.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  NULL AS `cis_TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `cis_HGN_CODE`,
  NULL AS `cis_GRADE_TYPE`,
  NULL AS `cis_TOTAL_UNITS`,
  NULL AS `cis_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  NULL AS `cis_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  NULL AS `drupal_TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `drupal_HGN_CODE`,
  NULL AS `drupal_GRADE_TYPE`,
  NULL AS `drupal_TOTAL_UNITS`,
  NULL AS `drupal_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  NULL AS `drupal_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered` cso
JOIN `academic_terms` at
  ON (cso.`TERM_CODE` = at.`TERM_CODE` OR cso.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = at.`TERM_CODE`)
WHERE at.`IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'Y'

UNION ALL

SELECT
  NULL AS `TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `HGN_CODE`,
  NULL AS `GRADE_TYPE`,
  NULL AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  NULL AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  NULL AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  cis.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `cis_TERM_CODE`,  -- keep original column name source; term code not stored so using ACADEMIC_YEAR as the canonical term-like column in cis
  cis.`HGN_CODE` AS `cis_HGN_CODE`,
  cis.`GRADE_TYPE` AS `cis_GRADE_TYPE`,
  cis.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `cis_TOTAL_UNITS`,
  cis.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `cis_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  cis.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `cis_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  NULL AS `drupal_TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `drupal_HGN_CODE`,
  NULL AS `drupal_GRADE_TYPE`,
  NULL AS `drupal_TOTAL_UNITS`,
  NULL AS `drupal_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  NULL AS `drupal_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  cis.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SECTION`
FROM `cis_course_catalog` cis
JOIN `academic_terms` at2
  ON (cis.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = at2.`TERM_CODE` OR cis.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` = at2.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`)
WHERE at2.`IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'Y'

UNION ALL

SELECT
  NULL AS `TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `HGN_CODE`,
  NULL AS `GRADE_TYPE`,
  NULL AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  NULL AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  NULL AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  NULL AS `cis_TERM_CODE`,
  NULL AS `cis_HGN_CODE`,
  NULL AS `cis_GRADE_TYPE`,
  NULL AS `cis_TOTAL_UNITS`,
  NULL AS `cis_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  NULL AS `cis_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  dr.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `drupal_TERM_CODE`,  -- drupal stores academic year/term info in ACADEMIC_YEAR and SO_TERM_CODE; include ACADEMIC_YEAR here as term-like column
  dr.`HGN_CODE` AS `drupal_HGN_CODE`,
  dr.`GRADE_TYPE` AS `drupal_GRADE_TYPE`,
  dr.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `drupal_TOTAL_UNITS`,
  dr.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `drupal_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  dr.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS `drupal_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  dr.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION`
FROM `drupal_course_catalog` dr
JOIN `academic_terms` at3
  ON (dr.`SO_TERM_CODE` = at3.`TERM_CODE` OR dr.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = at3.`TERM_CODE` OR dr.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` = at3.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`)
WHERE at3.`IS_CURRENT_TERM` = 'Y'
course_offers_current_term.description: All course-offer rows for the current term from canonical course-offer/catalog sources (primary: course_catalog_subject_offered; fallbacks: cis_course_catalog, drupal_course_catalog). Includes term code, HGN code, grade/type and total units, department/subject and responsible faculty id; filtered to rows whose TERM_CODE/EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE matches a current term.

subject_department_mapping.name: subject_department_mapping
subject_department_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT

subject_department_mapping.description: Mapping of each subject (subject_id or subject_code) to its department unit (org id / department id). One row per subject-to-department mapping; prefer mappings present in cis_course_catalog or course_catalog_subject_offered.

tip_subject_course.name: tip_subject_course

tip_material_school_links.name: tip_material_school_links
tip_material_school_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through a stable material identifier from tip_material
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS `material_id`,
  -- school/vendor identifier: use MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE as the source of school/vendor id
  -- (kept as-is from base table to satisfy "do NOT substitute or re-derive")
  `tip_material`.`MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE` AS `school_id`
FROM
  `tip_material`
WHERE
  -- ensure distinct mapping by filtering out NULL/empty sources; deduplication is handled
  -- by selection of unique pairs at view consumption time. Here we remove obviously blank keys.
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` <> ''
  AND `tip_material`.`MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `tip_material`.`MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE` <> ''
GROUP BY
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`,
  `tip_material`.`MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE`
tip_material_school_links.description: Normalized mapping of each TIP material record to its associated school/vendor identifiers; one row per material_id x school_id. Ensures distinct school identifiers per material.

material_status_lookup.name: material_status_lookup
material_status_lookup.body_sql:

FROM

UNION
SELECT

material_schools.name: material_schools

subject_offerings_term_level.name: subject_offerings_term_level
subject_offerings_term_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  `subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE`                    AS `term_code`,
  `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY`  AS `subject_offered_id`,
  `subject_offered`.`OFFER_DEPT_CODE`              AS `department`,
  -- try to return numeric enrolled where possible: prefer NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS (int),
  -- fall back to SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER (int) then SECTION_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER (varchar parsed)
  COALESCE(
    `subject_offered`.`NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS`,
    `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER`,
    -- parse SECTION_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER to integer when it contains digits; NULL if not numeric
    NULLIF(
      TRIM(
        -- remove non-digit characters at ends; keep interior digits. Use regex-like replace via REPLACE chains is limited,
        -- but attempt safe CAST: CAST will return 0 on non-numeric strings in MySQL strict mode it errors; use +0 trick
        `subject_offered`.`SECTION_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER`
      ), ''
    ) + 0
  ) AS `enrolled`
FROM `subject_offered`
subject_offerings_term_level.description: All subject/offering rows (one row per subject-offering record) with term code, department/school identifier, and numeric enrollment parsed where possible; serves as the primary set of rows to count total records per term.

tip_items_by_term.name: tip_items_by_term
tip_items_by_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  tso.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY) AS tip_subjects_offered_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS tip_materials_needed_count
FROM tip_subject_offered tso
LEFT JOIN tip_detail td
  ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  AND td.TERM_CODE = tso.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms
  ON tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
GROUP BY
  tso.TERM_CODE
tip_items_by_term.description: Aggregated counts of TIP subjects offered and TIP materials needed per term code. Detects TIP flags/columns and counts flagged subject records and counts material rows linked to subjects for each term.

schools_per_term.name: schools_per_term
schools_per_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.TERM_CODE AS `term_code`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE) AS `department`
FROM
  subject_offered AS so
WHERE
  so.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  so.TERM_CODE
schools_per_term.description: Count of distinct non-null department/school identifiers offering subjects per term code.

SELECT

term_rows.name: term_rows
term_rows.description: All academic term rows (one per term code) with canonical term code and description to be used as the term/cohort filter. This isolates term metadata (code and description) for any term.

subject_offering_rows.name: subject_offering_rows
subject_offering_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  `TERM_CODE`,
  `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `PREREQUISITES`,
  `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
FROM (
  -- source: course_catalog_subject_offered
  SELECT
    `TERM_CODE`,
    `SUBJECT_CODE`,
    `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    `PREREQUISITES`,
    `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
  FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`

  UNION ALL

  -- source: drupal_course_catalog
  SELECT
    `SO_TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
    `SUBJECT_CODE`,
    `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    `PREREQUISITES`,
    `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
  FROM `drupal_course_catalog`

  UNION ALL

  -- source: cis_course_catalog
  -- cis table does not store a TERM_CODE column in the DDL; include NULL for TERM_CODE to preserve schema.
  SELECT
    NULL AS `TERM_CODE`,
    `SUBJECT_CODE`,
    `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    `PREREQUISITES`,
    NULL AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
  FROM `cis_course_catalog`
) AS unified_subject_offerings
subject_offering_rows.description: Unioned rows of subject/course offerings from the course-catalog sources. One row per catalog record (a subject-offering instance) including its term, subject code, subject title, prerequisites, and responsible faculty name. This canonicalizes columns across course_catalog_subject_offered, drupal_course_catalog, and cis_course_catalog so downstream logic treats them uniformly.

rooms_core.name: rooms_core
rooms_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME AS ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY     AS BUILDING_ID,
  fr.FLOOR_KEY        AS FLOOR_ID,
  -- SQFT_ASSIGNABLE: use stored AREA from fac_rooms, cast/clean to numeric
  CASE
    WHEN fr.AREA IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(CAST(fr.AREA AS CHAR)) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(fr.AREA AS DECIMAL(18,2))
  END AS SQFT_ASSIGNABLE,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY AS OCCUPANT_ORG_ID,
  fr.DEPT_CODE        AS DEPT_CODE,
  -- grain identifier carried through so view remains joinable
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY     AS ROOM_ID
FROM fac_rooms fr
-- exclude rows lacking a room identifier (ROOM is the room identifier per grain ROOM_ID is FAC_ROOM_KEY;
-- also exclude null/empty ROOM value to ensure a room exists)
WHERE fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(COALESCE(fr.ROOM,'')) <> ''
rooms_core.description: Canonical room-level rows with core identifying fields and numeric room area, including building and floor keys and occupying org/department codes. Clean/cast area to numeric and exclude rows lacking a room identifier.

floor_assignable_area.name: floor_assignable_area
floor_assignable_area.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_floor`.`FLOOR_KEY` AS `FLOOR_ID`,
  `fac_floor`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_ID`,
  SUM(`fac_rooms`.`AREA`) AS `SQFT_ASSIGNABLE_FLOOR`
FROM `fac_floor`
LEFT JOIN `fac_rooms`
  ON `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` = `fac_floor`.`BUILDING_KEY`
  AND `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR_KEY` = `fac_floor`.`FLOOR_KEY`
GROUP BY
  `fac_floor`.`FLOOR_KEY`,
  `fac_floor`.`BUILDING_KEY`
floor_assignable_area.description: Per-floor total assignable area (sum of assignable areas of rooms on that floor).

building_assignable_area.name: building_assignable_area
building_assignable_area.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_ID,
  fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA      AS ASSIGNABLE_SQFT
FROM fac_building fb
building_assignable_area.description: Per-building total assignable square footage (building-level aggregate of assignable area across floors/rooms).

room_basic_attrs.name: room_basic_attrs
room_basic_attrs.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical room identifier (grain)
  `FAC_ROOM_KEY`                AS `ROOM_ID`,

  -- room full name (use stored column)
  `ROOM_FULL_NAME`              AS `ROOM_FULL_NAME`,

  -- room area (use stored AREA)
  `AREA`                        AS `ROOM_AREA`,

  -- floor identifier from fac_rooms (stored)
  `FLOOR`                       AS `FLOOR`,

  -- building identifier from fac_rooms (stored)
  `BUILDING_KEY`                AS `BUILDING`,

  -- occupying organization code (use stored ORGANIZATION_KEY)
  `ORGANIZATION_KEY`            AS `OCCUPying_ORG_CODE`,

  -- occupying department code (use stored DEPT_CODE)
  `DEPT_CODE`                   AS `OCCUPying_DEPT_CODE`

FROM
  `fac_rooms`
WHERE
  -- filter out rows missing core non-null attributes required for downstream area/share calculations
  `FAC_ROOM_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND `ROOM_FULL_NAME` IS NOT NULL
  AND `AREA` IS NOT NULL
  AND `FLOOR` IS NOT NULL
  AND `BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND `ORGANIZATION_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND `DEPT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
room_basic_attrs.description: One row per room with canonicalized room identifiers and core attributes needed for area/share calculations (room id/full name, room area, floor identifier, building identifier, occupying organization and department identifiers/names). Filters out rows missing core non-null attributes.

building_gross_area.name: building_gross_area
building_gross_area.body_sql:

  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING,
  fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA AS GROSS_SQUARE_FEET
FROM fac_building fb
building_gross_area.description: Total building area (gross square feet or equivalent) used as denominator to compute percent of building area. One row per building with its gross area.

building_name_lookup.name: building_name_lookup
building_name_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME
FROM buildings b
-- ensure only buildings that exist in buildings are included;
-- allow joining to the latest facility record when available to prefer canonical name,
-- but do not substitute stored buildings columns. Left join so BUILDING_NAME still comes from buildings.
LEFT JOIN rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key r
  ON r.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
building_name_lookup.description: Mapping of building identifier to canonical building name for display; used to ensure only buildings present in the buildings table are included.

building_departments.name: building_departments
building_departments.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY        AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.COST_CENTER_CODE        AS DEPT_CODE,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME      AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME       AS HR_ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY        AS FCLT_ORGANIZATION_BUILDING_KEY
FROM fac_building fb
JOIN fac_organization fo
  ON fb.COST_CENTER_CODE = fo.D_CODE
building_departments.description: Map buildings to departments (department names) and organizations when such relationships are available in facility/organization tables. Produces one row per building-department/organization association. If a direct mapping is not present for a building, rows may be absent (caller will left-join to buildings).

org_names_by_dept.name: org_names_by_dept
org_names_by_dept.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.D_CODE AS DEPT_CODE,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS HR_ORGANIZATION_NAME
FROM fac_organization fo
-- Normalize/choose a canonical name per department code by selecting distinct dept codes.
-- If multiple rows exist for same D_CODE, the view exposes the values from fac_organization;
-- downstream queries should aggregate/choose preferred row as needed.
GROUP BY fo.D_CODE, fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME, fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME
org_names_by_dept.description: Normalize and deduplicate organization/department names by department code (one row per department code) to provide canonical HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME and HR_ORGANIZATION_NAME for joins and final aggregation.

fall_subject_instructor_pairs.name: fall_subject_instructor_pairs
fall_subject_instructor_pairs.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY       AS SUBJ_INST_ID,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE             AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  so.TERM_CODE                 AS TERM_CODE,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME  AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  d.MIT_ID                     AS MIT_ID,
  d.EMAIL_ADDRESS              AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  d.FULL_NAME                  AS FULL_NAME
FROM subject_offered so
LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory d
  ON (so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID <> ''
      AND d.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND d.MIT_ID <> ''
      AND so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = d.MIT_ID)
UNION
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY       AS SUBJ_INST_ID,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE             AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  so.TERM_CODE                 AS TERM_CODE,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME  AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  d.MIT_ID                     AS MIT_ID,
  d.EMAIL_ADDRESS              AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  d.FULL_NAME                  AS FULL_NAME
FROM subject_offered so
JOIN drupal_employee_directory d
  ON ( (so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID IS NULL OR so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = '')
       AND so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
       AND so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME <> ''
       AND d.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL
       AND d.FULL_NAME <> ''
       AND so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME = d.FULL_NAME )
UNION
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY       AS SUBJ_INST_ID,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE             AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  so.TERM_CODE                 AS TERM_CODE,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME  AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  d.MIT_ID                     AS MIT_ID,
  d.EMAIL_ADDRESS              AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  d.FULL_NAME                  AS FULL_NAME
FROM subject_offered so
JOIN drupal_employee_directory d
  ON ( (so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID IS NULL OR so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = '')
       AND so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
       AND so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME <> ''
       AND d.FIRST_NAME IS NOT NULL
       AND d.LAST_NAME IS NOT NULL
       AND CONCAT(d.FIRST_NAME, ' ', d.LAST_NAME) = so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME )
WHERE (EMAIL_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND EMAIL_ADDRESS <> '')
fall_subject_instructor_pairs.description: Join fall subject offerings to instructor directory to attach an instructor email. Join primarily on RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = MIT_ID; fallback join keys include matching RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME to directory FULL_NAME or FIRST_NAME + ' ' + LAST_NAME. Only retain rows where an email address could be resolved.

instructor_fall_subject_counts.name: instructor_fall_subject_counts

building_sqft_aggregates.name: building_sqft_aggregates

responsible_faculty_contact.name: responsible_faculty_contact
