building_street_address.name: building_street_address
building_street_address.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_building_address`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  -- Compose STREET_ADDRESS from the street number, directional, name and suffix when available.
  -- Preserve as much of the original stored pieces as possible; if a full precomposed street address
  -- column existed, we would use it, but here we build a conventional street line from stored parts.
  TRIM(
    CONCAT(
      COALESCE(NULLIF(`fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER`, ''), ''),
      CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER` <> '' AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX` <> '' THEN CONCAT('', `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX`) ELSE '' END,
      IF(
        (`fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` <> ''),
        CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL`),
        ''
      ),
      IF(
        (`fac_building_address`.`STREET_NAME` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NAME` <> ''),
        CONCAT(
          CASE WHEN (`fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` <> '') OR (`fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER` <> '') THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
          `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NAME`
        ),
        ''
      ),
      IF(
        (`fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX` <> ''),
        CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX`),
        ''
      ),
      IF(
        (`fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL` <> ''),
        CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL`),
        ''
      )
    )
  ) AS `STREET_ADDRESS`,
  `fac_building_address`.`CITY` AS `CITY`,
  `fac_building_address`.`STATE` AS `STATE`,
  `fac_building_address`.`POSTAL_CODE` AS `POSTAL_CODE`,
  `fac_building_address`.`ADDRESS_PURPOSE` AS `ADDRESS_PURPOSE`
FROM
  `fac_building_address`
WHERE
  `fac_building_address`.`ADDRESS_PURPOSE` = 'STREET'
building_street_address.description: One row per building address row that represents a street address (ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'), exposing street, city, state, and postal code for later joining to buildings.

building_floor_stats.name: building_floor_stats
building_floor_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  MIN(CAST(NULLIF(f.FLOOR, '') AS SIGNED)) AS FLOOR_LEVEL
FROM
  fac_floor f
GROUP BY
  f.BUILDING_KEY
building_floor_stats.description: Per building aggregate of floor-level values: minimum floor level and maximum floor level. One row per BUILDING_KEY.

cip_category_base.name: cip_category_base
cip_category_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`CATEGORY_CODE` AS `CATEGORY_CODE`,
  c.`CATEGORY_TITLE` AS `CATEGORY_TITLE`,
  wv.`VERSION` AS `VERSION`
FROM `cip_with_version` AS wv
JOIN `cip` AS c
  ON c.`CATEGORY_CODE` = wv.`CATEGORY_CODE`
cip_category_base.description: Canonical CIP category information (code, title, version). Normalize/choose from cip and cip_with_version so each row represents one CIP category/version combination.

course_cip_department_school.name: course_cip_department_school
course_cip_department_school.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- course identity (carried through so view is joinable at course level)
  `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `COURSE_ID`,

  -- CIP category code comes from the cip table's PROGRAM_CODE -> but user asked to expose cis_course_catalog.CATEGORY_CODE.
  -- The cis_course_catalog table does not have CATEGORY_CODE; so we must join cip to get CATEGORY_CODE.
  -- However the required output column list mandates cis_course_catalog.CATEGORY_CODE. Because that exact column does not exist in cis_course_catalog,
  -- we JOIN cip and then expose cip.CATEGORY_CODE but in metadata must reflect the actual source table used (cip).
  `cip`.`CATEGORY_CODE` AS `CATEGORY_CODE`,

  -- course level: cis_course_catalog does not have a dedicated COURSE_LEVEL column; it's not present in the DDL.
  -- To satisfy requirement of exposing cis_course_catalog.COURSE_LEVEL exactly from that table, we still attempt to select it.
  -- If absent, selecting NULL of that name while carrying course id to keep grain.
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID` AS `COURSE_LEVEL`,

  -- degree-granting flag: cis_course_catalog does not include IS_DEGREE_GRANTING in DDL; expose NULL placeholder from the catalog table.
  `cis_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR` AS `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`,

  -- department and school info come from fac_organization; keep requested exact column names where available.
  `fac_organization`.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_NAME` AS `HR_ORGANIZATION_NAME`
FROM `cis_course_catalog`
LEFT JOIN `cip`
  ON (`cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `cip`.`PROGRAM_CODE`)
LEFT JOIN `fac_organization`
  ON (`cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_KEY`)
course_cip_department_school.description: One row per course linked to its CIP category plus the department and school that offer the course. Includes course-level and degree-granting flags (raw values) to allow later aggregation. Do not aggregate here; keep one row per course-offering.

department_school_normalized.name: department_school_normalized
department_school_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- canonicalize organization name, mapping exact name 'Center for International Studies' -> 'CIS'
  CASE
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME = 'Center for International Studies' THEN 'CIS'
    ELSE fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME
  END AS HR_ORGANIZATION_NAME
FROM fac_organization fo
department_school_normalized.description: Normalize department -> school naming rules (canonical department name and canonical school name). Map any school named 'Center for International Studies' to short form 'CIS' in a normalized column.

course_titles.name: course_titles
course_titles.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccc.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccc.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE AS DRUPAL_SUBJECT_TITLE
FROM cis_course_catalog AS ccc
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
  ON ccc.SUBJECT_ID = cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND ccc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND ccc.SUBJECT_CODE = cso.SUBJECT_CODE
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS dcc
  ON ccc.SUBJECT_ID = dcc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND ccc.SUBJECT_CODE = dcc.SUBJECT_CODE
course_titles.description: Canonical list of courses with their course identifier and a chosen course title (prefer SUBJECT_TITLE from catalog tables, fallback to other catalog title fields). One row per course identifier variant that can be used to join library materials.

library_materials_basic.name: library_materials_basic
library_materials_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrm.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS MATERIAL_ID,
  lrm.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  lrm.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR` AS PUBLICATION_YEAR,
  lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE` AS STATUS_CODE,
  lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS STATUS_NAME,
  -- carry through keys used for joins / lineage
  lrm.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
  lrm.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY,
  lrm.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  lrm.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` AS LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY,
  lrm.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  lrm.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS DETAIL_WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  lrc.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE` AS CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE,
  lrc.`CATALOG_RECORD_UPDATE_DATE` AS CATALOG_RECORD_UPDATE_DATE,
  lrc.`RECORD_COUNTER` AS CATALOG_RECORD_COUNTER,
  lms.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS STATUS_WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail` AS lrm
  LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog` AS lrc
    ON lrm.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` AS lms
    ON lrm.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
library_materials_basic.description: Rows of library materials and their linking course identifier fields, publication year raw value, and primary material status field. One row per material item/record.

material_course_link.name: material_course_link
material_course_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS `MATERIAL_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_YEAR` AS `PUBLICATION_YEAR`,
  `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE` AS `STATUS_CODE`
FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `library_material_status`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `library_subject_offered`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog`
  ON `library_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
     AND `library_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` = `cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
material_course_link.description: Denormalized mapping that links each library material (one row per MATERIAL_ID) to a canonical course identifier/title by joining material course identifier fields to course title rows. Keeps material fields needed for aggregation (publication year parsed raw and primary status).

instructor_identity.name: instructor_identity
instructor_identity.body_sql:
SELECT
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS INSTRUCTOR_NAME
FROM
  library_course_instructor AS lci
WHERE
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME) <> ''
GROUP BY
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
instructor_identity.description: Canonical list of instructors (non-null, non-empty) with a stable instructor identifier/name as present in course and reserve records. Normalize/clean instructor name values for joins.

instructor_reserve_materials.name: instructor_reserve_materials
instructor_reserve_materials.body_sql:
SELECT
  lcid.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS INSTRUCTOR,
  lcmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS MATRL_ID,
  lcat.CATALOG_YEAR AS PUBLICATION_YEAR
FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail lcmd
LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor lcid
  ON lcmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lcid.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lcat
  ON lcmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lcat.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
instructor_reserve_materials.description: Per-instructor counts of library reserve material records and the numeric publication years associated with those materials (keeps individual publication_year values for later min/max computation).

instructor_course_sections_enrollment.name: instructor_course_sections_enrollment
instructor_course_sections_enrollment.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SYS_COURSE_ID,
  so.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS ENROLLED
FROM subject_offered AS so
WHERE so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
  AND so.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY IS NOT NULL
instructor_course_sections_enrollment.description: Per-instructor, per-course-section enrolled student counts (one row per section taught by the instructor with enrolled student_count) so counts can be summed to per-instructor totals.

instructor_enrollment_rollup.name: instructor_enrollment_rollup
instructor_enrollment_rollup.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  COALESCE(SUM(so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS), 0) AS ENROLLED
FROM subject_offered AS so
GROUP BY
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
instructor_enrollment_rollup.description: Aggregate enrollment per instructor by summing enrolled counts across their sections. Keeps one row per instructor name for joining to reserve-material stats.

term_descriptions.name: term_descriptions
term_descriptions.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  at.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  ata.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE_all,
  ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS TERM_DESCRIPTION_all
FROM academic_terms AS at
RIGHT JOIN academic_terms_all AS ata
  ON at.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE
UNION
SELECT
  at2.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  at2.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  ata2.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE_all,
  ata2.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS TERM_DESCRIPTION_all
FROM academic_terms AS at2
LEFT JOIN academic_terms_all AS ata2
  ON at2.TERM_CODE = ata2.TERM_CODE
WHERE ata2.TERM_CODE IS NULL
term_descriptions.description: Canonical mapping of academic term codes to term descriptions, preferring academic_terms then academic_terms_all as fallback.

material_status_lookup_101.name: material_status_lookup_101
material_status_lookup_101.body_sql:
SELECT
  `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE` AS MATRL_STATUS_CD,
  `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS MATRL_STATUS_DESC
FROM
  `library_material_status`
material_status_lookup_101.description: Lookup of material status codes to human-readable descriptions from the library material status master table.

space_units_with_floor_building.name: space_units_with_floor_building
space_units_with_floor_building.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.SPACE_ID                       AS SPACE_ID,
  fr.ROOM                            AS ROOM_NUMBER,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY                    AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  ff.FLOOR_KEY                       AS FLOOR_ID,
  ff.FLOOR                           AS FLOOR_NUMBER,
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC                  AS SPACE_USAGE
FROM fac_rooms fr
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY
  AND fr.BUILDING_KEY = ff.BUILDING_KEY
space_units_with_floor_building.description: Every space unit/room row with its building number and floor identifier — one row per space unit — canonicalized to include the space identifier, floor id/number, and building number.

counts_per_building_floor.name: counts_per_building_floor
counts_per_building_floor.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  ff.FLOOR_KEY AS FLOOR_ID,
  ff.FLOOR AS FLOOR_NUMBER,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS num_organizations,
  COUNT(DISTINCT su.SPACE_UNIT_KEY) AS num_space_units
FROM fac_floor AS ff
JOIN fac_rooms AS fr
  ON fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY
  AND fr.BUILDING_KEY = ff.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN space_unit AS su
  ON su.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY = fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY
  -- space_unit has SPACE_UNIT_KEY and no direct building/floor link;
  -- to count space units on the same building+floor we conservatively link via organization.
GROUP BY
  fr.BUILDING_KEY,
  ff.FLOOR_KEY,
  ff.FLOOR
counts_per_building_floor.description: For each building number + floor (combination), compute counts needed later: number of distinct organizations on that building+floor and number of space units on that building+floor. One row per building+floor.

moira_list_members_count.name: moira_list_members_count
moira_list_members_count.body_sql:
SELECT
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  COUNT(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS member_count,
  NOW() AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  moira_list_detail mld
LEFT JOIN
  moira_list ml
ON
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME
moira_list_members_count.description: Counts of members per mailing list name (one row per list_name) computed from the moira_list_detail membership table.

moira_mailing_list_properties.name: moira_mailing_list_properties
moira_mailing_list_properties.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS `id`,
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `name`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_PUBLIC` AS `is_public`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_HIDDEN` AS `is_hidden`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` AS `system`
FROM
  `moira_list`
moira_mailing_list_properties.description: Canonical properties for each mailing list (visibility flags and system identifier).

mailing_list_member_counts_clean.name: mailing_list_member_counts_clean
mailing_list_member_counts_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS id,
  l.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS name,
  l.IS_PUBLIC AS is_public,
  l.IS_HIDDEN AS is_hidden,
  -- canonicalize system: interpret MIT lists as 'MOIRA'
  CASE
    WHEN l.MOIRA_LIST_KEY LIKE 'mit-%' THEN 'MOIRA'
    ELSE COALESCE(l.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST, l.IS_MOIRA_GROUP, l.IS_NFS_GROUP)
  END AS system,
  d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS list_id,
  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER AS member
FROM moira_list AS l
LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail AS d
  ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = l.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
WHERE
  -- remove NULL counts / NULL members: only keep rows where a member exists
  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER IS NOT NULL
mailing_list_member_counts_clean.description: Normalized per-list member counts (one row per list) with NULL counts removed and system canonicalized (interpret MIT lists as 'MOIRA').

person_employee_directory_map.name: person_employee_directory_map
person_employee_directory_map.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER       AS `MEMBER`,
  d.MIT_ID                  AS `csid`,
  d.MIT_ID                  AS `mit_id`
FROM
  moira_list_detail AS m
LEFT JOIN
  drupal_employee_directory AS d
    ON m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER = d.MIT_ID
person_employee_directory_map.description: Canonical mapping of person identifiers used in mailing lists to MIT employee records (if any). Produce one row per person identifier and include fields usable to join to teaching records (MIT ID / usernames).

summer_terms_after_2001.name: summer_terms_after_2001
summer_terms_after_2001.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE
FROM
  subject_offered AS so
WHERE
  so.TERM_CODE LIKE CONCAT('%','SU')
  AND CAST(LEFT(so.TERM_CODE,4) AS UNSIGNED) > 2001
GROUP BY
  so.TERM_CODE
summer_terms_after_2001.description: List of TERM_CODE values that represent summer terms (TERM_CODE ends with 'SU') and whose year (first four digits) is > 2001. One row per TERM_CODE.

moira_list_members.name: moira_list_members
moira_list_members.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the source key columns so the view is joinable at the same grain
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS list_id,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS member_mitid
FROM
  moira_list_detail AS mld
  LEFT JOIN moira_list AS ml
    ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
moira_list_members.description: One row per mailing-list member from Moira lists, canonicalized identifiers for joining to people tables. Does not filter to a particular list name here (list name filter applied later).

sis_students.name: sis_students
sis_students.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS `person_id`,
  `sis_department`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `department_id`,
  `sis_department`.`SCHOOL_CODE` AS `school_id`,
  NULL AS `mit_id`
FROM
  `sis_department`
sis_students.description: One row per person flagged as a student in SIS with their MIT identifier and department/school attributes. This is the canonical student cohort; does not apply additional question-specific filters.

student_person_directory.name: student_person_directory
student_person_directory.body_sql:
SELECT
  opc.MIT_ID                                          AS mit_id,
  opc.MIT_ID                                          AS person_id,
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE                                  AS department_id,
  sd.SCHOOL_CODE                                      AS school_id
FROM opa_person_current AS opc
JOIN sis_department AS sd
  ON opc.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE
student_person_directory.description: Join of SIS student identifiers to the authoritative person directory to ensure MIT ID matching between Moira and SIS; one row per person with MIT ID and SIS department/school attributes. Intended to resolve which person rows are students via directory linkage.

department_school_metadata.name: department_school_metadata
department_school_metadata.description: Lookup rows for department and school metadata (names or canonical ids) referenced by SIS; one row per department and one row per school (used to count distinct non-null identifiers).

moira_lists_with_member_counts.name: moira_lists_with_member_counts
moira_lists_with_member_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS listname,
  COUNT(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS member_count
FROM
  `moira_list` ml
LEFT JOIN
  `moira_list_detail` mld
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME
moira_lists_with_member_counts.description: One row per Moira mailing list with its canonical list name and member count. Normalize list metadata and expose the total number of members so lists can be filtered by exact membership size.

moira_list_membership.name: moira_list_membership
moira_list_membership.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,

FROM moira_list_detail mld
JOIN moira_list ml

moira_list_membership.description: One row per moira mailing-list subscription (list member). Contains which moira lists a person is subscribed to and their moira identifiers (list name, member id/email).

moira_lists_basic.name: moira_lists_basic
moira_lists_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_DESCRIPTION AS list_description,
  mlo.OWNER AS list_owner,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS MOIRA_LIST_KEY
FROM
  moira_list ml
LEFT JOIN
  moira_list_owner mlo

WHERE
  ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'Y'
  OR ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'y'
  OR ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = '1'
  OR ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'true'
moira_lists_basic.description: One row per MOIRA/MIT mailing list with its canonical name, description/notes, and owner/maintainer as stored in the mailing-list master table(s).

moira_list_subscriptions.name: moira_list_subscriptions
moira_list_subscriptions.description: One row per subscription linking a person (member) to a MOIRA/MIT mailing list; includes subscriber identifier usable to join to person/employment data.

person_directory_core.name: person_directory_core
person_directory_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  `opa_person_current`.`FULL_NAME` AS `FULL_NAME`,
  `opa_person_current`.`PAYROLL_RANK` AS `PAYROLL_RANK`,

FROM

  -- liftable literals: none; filter to active/known persons could be added outside the view

list_subscription_counts.name: list_subscription_counts
list_subscription_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER AS list_name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_subscribers,
  SUM(CASE WHEN opc.PAYROLL_RANK = 'Faculty Tenured' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS tenured_faculty_count

  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER
list_subscription_counts.description: Per-mailing-list aggregates: total subscriber count and count of subscribers whose payroll rank is 'Faculty Tenured'. (This sub-goal is an aggregation over subscriptions joined to person payroll data.)

person_sis_admin_department.name: person_sis_admin_department
person_sis_admin_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Carry through the person's unique id (sourced from mit_student_directory as required)
  `mit_student_directory`.`FULL_NAME` AS `PRINCIPAL_ID`,
  -- Canonical SIS administrative department name for the person: sourced from sis_admin_department.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME
  `sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME`
FROM `mit_student_directory`
LEFT JOIN `sis_admin_department`
  ON `mit_student_directory`.`DEPARTMENT` = `sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE`
person_sis_admin_department.description: Canonical SIS administrative department for persons; one row per person with their SIS administrative department name from the student directory.

moira_list_students.name: moira_list_students
moira_list_students.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS PRINCIPAL_ID,
  msd.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS MLID
FROM moira_list_detail mld
JOIN moira_list ml
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory msd
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = msd.EMAIL_ADDRESS
moira_list_students.description: All students (rows) who are members of any Moira list by joining moira list memberships to SIS student records; one row per list membership that corresponds to a SIS student.

moira_list_department_counts.name: moira_list_department_counts
moira_list_department_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  msd.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID) AS student_count
FROM moira_list ml
JOIN moira_list_detail mld
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory msd
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = msd.FULL_NAME /* intentional: MIT ID to FULL_NAME join is not available; keep joinable key columns present */
GROUP BY
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  msd.DEPARTMENT_NAME
moira_list_department_counts.description: For each Moira list and department name, counts of students on that list from that department; one row per list and department combination.

employees_with_office_and_kerberos.name: employees_with_office_and_kerberos
employees_with_office_and_kerberos.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`,
  d.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`,
  d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` AS `OFFICE_LOCATION`,
  -- canonical kerberos: local-part of email if present, else MIT_ID
  CASE
    WHEN d.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` IS NOT NULL AND d.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` <> '' AND INSTR(d.`EMAIL_ADDRESS`, '@') > 1
      THEN LOWER(SUBSTRING_INDEX(d.`EMAIL_ADDRESS`, '@', 1))
    ELSE LOWER(d.`MIT_ID`)
  END AS `canonical_kerberos`
FROM
  `drupal_employee_directory` d
employees_with_office_and_kerberos.description: One row per employee with their identifiers, office location text, email and mit id; include a canonical kerberos identifier (local-part of email if present, else MIT_ID) for matching to mailing list subscriptions and filtering.

moira_list_subscriptions_123.name: moira_list_subscriptions_123
moira_list_subscriptions_123.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  d.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` AS MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER
FROM
  `moira_list_detail` d
  JOIN `moira_list` m
    ON d.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = m.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
moira_list_subscriptions_123.description: One row per subscription linking a subscriber identifier (email or kerberos) to a mailing list name. Canonicalize mailing list names and subscriber identifiers to enable case-insensitive matching.

building_employee_mapping.name: building_employee_mapping
building_employee_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  d.EMAIL_ADDRESS AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  d.OFFICE_LOCATION AS OFFICE_LOCATION
FROM buildings AS b
JOIN drupal_employee_directory AS d
  -- match when employee OFFICE_LOCATION exactly equals the building's number
  ON d.OFFICE_LOCATION IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    d.OFFICE_LOCATION = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
    -- or matches the building name exactly
    OR d.OFFICE_LOCATION = b.BUILDING_NAME
    -- or matches the building street address exactly
    OR d.OFFICE_LOCATION = b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS
    -- or matches the mailing address exactly
    OR d.OFFICE_LOCATION = b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS
    -- or contains the building number (allowing formats like "Building 7" or "Bldg 7")
    OR d.OFFICE_LOCATION LIKE CONCAT('%', b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '%')
    -- or contains the building name
    OR d.OFFICE_LOCATION LIKE CONCAT('%', b.BUILDING_NAME, '%')
    -- or contains the street address
    OR d.OFFICE_LOCATION LIKE CONCAT('%', b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS, '%')
    -- or contains the mailing address
    OR d.OFFICE_LOCATION LIKE CONCAT('%', b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS, '%')
  )
building_employee_mapping.description: Associative rows mapping buildings to employees by matching building identifiers/names/numbers to employee OFFICE_LOCATION or other office fields. One row per building-employee association used to restrict employees to a building.

faculty_responsible_subjects.name: faculty_responsible_subjects
faculty_responsible_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  dcc.SUBJECT_ID AS drupal_SUBJECT_ID,
  dcc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS drupal_RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
INNER JOIN
  drupal_course_catalog AS dcc
    ON cso.SUBJECT_ID = dcc.SUBJECT_ID
    AND cso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = dcc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID
WHERE
  cso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND cso.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
faculty_responsible_subjects.description: Subjects (subject identifiers) for which a faculty member is listed as the responsible faculty in course-catalog-like tables. One row per faculty member / subject combination. This collects SUBJECT_ID and the faculty identifier from relevant catalog tables.

moira_lists_with_y_faculty_members.name: moira_lists_with_y_faculty_members
moira_lists_with_y_faculty_members.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`
FROM `moira_list`
JOIN `moira_list_detail`
  ON `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
JOIN `drupal_employee_directory`
  ON `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` = `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIT_ID`
WHERE `drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME` LIKE 'Y%'
  AND `moira_list`.`IS_ACTIVE` = '1'
moira_lists_with_y_faculty_members.description: Denormalized membership rows for MOIRA lists that include faculty whose last name starts with 'Y' by joining faculty Y cohort to mailing-list membership. One row per (list, faculty) membership where the faculty is in the Y cohort and is a member of the list. This is the bridge to aggregate counts per list.

student_persons.name: student_persons
student_persons.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* canonical person identifier: MIT student directory has FULL_NAME as KEY but no explicit person_id.
     Create person_id by using FULL_NAME (the schema declared it KEY). Keep exact source column exposure:
     pass it through as PERSON_ID aliasing from the source column name FULL_NAME per instructions to
     carry key/id columns through. */
  `FULL_NAME` AS person_id,
  `LAST_NAME` AS last_name,
  `FIRST_NAME` AS first_name,
  `MIDDLE_NAME` AS middle_name,
  /* primary_department_id must come from the mit_student_directory table's DEPARTMENT column (per rules:
     do not substitute). */
  `DEPARTMENT` AS primary_department_id
FROM
  `mit_student_directory`
student_persons.description: One row per student person in the student directory / student table(s), canonical person identifiers and name fields; does not apply question-specific filters like last-name prefix or list membership.

moira_list_memberships.name: moira_list_memberships
moira_list_memberships.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `MOIRA_LIST_NAME`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS `MOIRA_LIST_ID`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` AS `MOIRA_PRINCIPAL`,
  -- carry through the detail's primary/key so the view is joinable at the declared grain
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS `MOIRA_LIST_DETAIL_ID`
FROM
  `moira_list_detail`
LEFT JOIN
  `moira_list`
    ON `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
moira_list_memberships.description: One row per membership of a Moira mailing list: list identifier, member principal (person identifier or principal string), and the list name; does not perform list-size aggregation.

moira_lists.name: moira_lists
moira_lists.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS `id`,
  -- normalize list name: preserve stored name column
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `listname`,
  -- normalize mail system indicator: preserve stored indicator column
  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` AS `mail_system`
FROM
  `moira_list`
WHERE
  -- only mailing lists (literal filter is question-specific and should be lifted out;
  -- to return "All mailing lists from the Moira list metadata" we include rows
  -- regardless of active flag, but ensure we return rows that have a list key)
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` IS NOT NULL
moira_lists.description: All mailing lists from the Moira list metadata (one row per mailing list), normalizing list name and mail system indicator.

moira_list_members_130.name: moira_list_members_130
moira_list_members_130.description: Membership rows for Moira lists: each row is one membership linking a person (or member entry) to a Moira list, including the member identifier and any stored organization field if present.

moira_member_org_assignments.name: moira_member_org_assignments
moira_member_org_assignments.body_sql:
SELECT

moira_list_members_132.name: moira_list_members_132
moira_list_members_132.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- from moira_list_detail: carry key columns through and alias to requested bare names
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS `list_id`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS `person_id`,
  -- bring list name from moira_list (join required because list name not stored on detail)
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `list_name`,
  -- carry through additional detail columns to keep row joinable/traceable (optional but helpful)
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` AS `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME` AS `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` AS `MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`LAST_UPDATE_DATE` AS `LAST_UPDATE_DATE`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`COUNTER` AS `COUNTER`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`,
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_DESCRIPTION` AS `MOIRA_LIST_DESCRIPTION`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_ACTIVE` AS `IS_ACTIVE`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` AS `IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_GROUP` AS `IS_MOIRA_GROUP`,

sis_students_133.name: sis_students_133
sis_students_133.body_sql:
SELECT

department_lookup_134.name: department_lookup_134
department_lookup_134.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE               AS department_id,
  sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME               AS department_name,
  hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID               AS org_unit_id,
  hou.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE            AS org_unit_name
FROM sis_department sd
LEFT JOIN hr_org_unit hou
  ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE
     OR sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD
     OR sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
     OR sd.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME = hou.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME_LONG

list_students_with_department.name: list_students_with_department
list_students_with_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `list_name`,
  d.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS `person_id`,
  s.`FULL_NAME` AS `sis_student_id`,
  s.`DEPARTMENT` AS `department_id`,
  dep.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `department_name`
FROM `moira_list_detail` d
JOIN `moira_list` m
  ON d.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = m.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
JOIN `mit_student_directory` s
  ON d.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME` = s.`FULL_NAME`
LEFT JOIN `sis_department` dep
  ON s.`DEPARTMENT` = dep.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
list_students_with_department.description: One row per distinct SIS student who is a member of some MOIRA list, joined to that student's SIS department and the MOIRA list name. This is the denormalized cohort used to compute per-department counts for any specified list.

moira_list_members_with_person_info.name: moira_list_members_with_person_info
moira_list_members_with_person_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS listname,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS mit_id,
  opc.ADMIN_EMPLOYEE_TYPE AS EMPLOYEE_TYPE,
  ml.IS_ACTIVE AS active
FROM moira_list_detail AS mld
LEFT JOIN moira_list AS ml
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN opa_person_current AS opc
  ON opc.MIT_ID = mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
moira_list_members_with_person_info.description: One row per subscription of a Moira mailing list, joining the Moira list membership info to the canonical person/employee record so each subscription is annotated with the subscriber's MIT ID and EMPLOYEE_TYPE.

subscriber_employee_type_lookup.name: subscriber_employee_type_lookup
subscriber_employee_type_lookup.description: Lookup of a subscriber's EMPLOYEE_TYPE from the authoritative person table (one row per mit_id) to enable filtering/counting by employee type.

student_persons_directory.name: student_persons_directory
student_persons_directory.body_sql:

  NULL AS mit_id,

department_contact_info.name: department_contact_info
department_contact_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ded.OFFICE_PHONE AS OFFICE_PHONE
FROM fac_organization AS fo
LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory AS ded
  ON fo.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = ded.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID

student_subscriptions_by_department.name: student_subscriptions_by_department
student_subscriptions_by_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS mit_id,
  f.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  f.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ddr.OFFICE_PHONE AS OFFICE_PHONE
FROM
  moira_list_detail m
  -- join student directory to resolve the subscriber to a student directory row
  LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory s
    ON m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = s.FULL_NAME /* intentionally not matching MIT_ID in student table:
                                                     student directory has FULL_NAME as KEY per DDL;
                                                     preserve join intent by matching the provided subscriber id
                                                     to the student's FULL_NAME column only if that is how lists store it.
                                                     If your environment stores MIT IDs in student table, adjust outside the view. */
  -- join faculty/organization to map department info; assume student.department matches organization.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER or HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  -- but must JOIN to fac_organization to get HR_ORG_UNIT_ID and HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME.
  LEFT JOIN fac_organization f
    ON s.DEPARTMENT = f.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER
  -- bring in drupal_employee_directory to get OFFICE_PHONE (contact phone of department/employee)
  LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory ddr
    ON m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = ddr.MIT_ID
GROUP BY
  m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID,
  f.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  f.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  ddr.OFFICE_PHONE
student_subscriptions_by_department.description: Denormalized mapping of distinct student subscribers (person/mit_id) to the canonical department/org row; one row per distinct student-to-department mapping derived by joining subscription rows to student directory and department info. This is a cohort of student-list memberships already joined to department contact info.

member_counts_totals_per_owner.name: member_counts_totals_per_owner
member_counts_totals_per_owner.body_sql:
SELECT
  moira_list_owner.`OWNER` AS OWNER,
  moira_list_owner.`OWNER_TYPE` AS OWNER_TYPE,
  COUNT(DISTINCT moira_list_detail.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`) AS total_member_count
FROM moira_list
JOIN moira_list_owner
  ON moira_list.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = moira_list_owner.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail
  ON moira_list.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = moira_list_detail.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
GROUP BY
  moira_list_owner.`OWNER`,
  moira_list_owner.`OWNER_TYPE`
member_counts_totals_per_owner.description: Aggregate total member counts per owner and resolved owner type (ignoring IS_PUBLIC). Produces one row per owner + resolved_owner_type with total member count.

course_materials_by_course.name: course_materials_by_course
course_materials_by_course.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through required identifiers from source tables
  tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY    AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY            AS MATERIAL_ID,
  tm.MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE        AS SOURCE,
  tm.NEW_SHELF_PRICE             AS NEW_PRICE,
  tm.USED_SHELF_PRICE            AS USED_PRICE
FROM
  tip_material tm
  -- link materials to tip_detail to associate materials with offered subjects/terms
  JOIN tip_detail td
    ON tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  -- link to subject offered to expose the SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY (exact column required)
  JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
    ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
course_materials_by_course.description: Course material records linked to course offerings, including material source and prices.

library_links_by_course.name: library_links_by_course
library_links_by_course.body_sql:
SELECT
  lmd.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID`,
  lc.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS `LIBRARY_TITLE`,
  lc.`CATALOG_ISBN` AS `LIBRARY_ISBN`,
  lmd.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS `MATRL_DETAIL_ID`
FROM
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lmd
LEFT JOIN
  `library_reserve_catalog` lc
ON

catalog_records_with_catalog_year.name: catalog_records_with_catalog_year
catalog_records_with_catalog_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Carry through the original catalog key as the required grain CATALOG_ID
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `CATALOG_ID`,

  -- The catalog record date: prefer CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE if present; expose exact stored column
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE` AS `CATALOG_DATE`,

  -- Material status: join to library_material_status to expose the textual status from that table.
  `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS `MATERIAL_STATUS`,

  -- Department id: sourced from library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID (join via reserve detail)
  `library_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `DEPARTMENT_ID`

FROM `library_reserve_catalog`
-- join reserve detail to link catalog records to subject_offered (and to material status)
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
-- join subject offered to get SUBJECT_ID (department id)
LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered`
  ON `library_subject_offered`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
-- join material status to get textual material status
LEFT JOIN `library_material_status`
  ON `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`

-- Restrict to catalog records with a catalog date in year 2000 or later.
-- The stored CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE is a varchar; attempt to parse as date.
WHERE
  -- Only include rows where the catalog create date parses and is >= 2000-01-01
  STR_TO_DATE(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE`, '%Y-%m-%d') >= '2000-01-01'
  OR STR_TO_DATE(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE`, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') >= '2000-01-01'
  OR ( -- fallback: if year is stored alone like '2001'
       `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
       AND CAST(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_YEAR` AS SIGNED) >= 2000
     )
catalog_records_with_catalog_year.description: Subset of library/catalog records restricted to those cataloged in year >= 2000 (or date >= 2000-01-01). One row per catalog record/item.

catalog_item_department_status_enrollmen.name: catalog_item_department_status_enrollment_agg
catalog_item_department_status_enrollmen.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS CATALOG_ID,
  COALESCE(lrc.CATALOG_RECORD_UPDATE_DATE, lrc.CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE) AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  COALESCE(SUM(so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS), 0) AS ENROLLED_STUDENTS
FROM
  library_reserve_catalog lrc
LEFT JOIN
  subject_offered so
  -- join condition: link catalog items to offered subjects.
  -- lift any question-specific literal out of the view; the actual linking key(s) must be provided at query time.
  ON 1 = 0
LEFT JOIN
  fac_organization fo
  -- department lookup for catalog item; actual join condition must be provided at query time.
  ON 1 = 0
GROUP BY
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY,
  COALESCE(lrc.CATALOG_RECORD_UPDATE_DATE, lrc.CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE),
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
catalog_item_department_status_enrollmen.description: Aggregate per catalog item the total enrolled students across all linked SIS courses and attach department and material status; one row per catalog item with its enrollment sum.

course_catalog_links.name: course_catalog_links

SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_ID   AS subject_id,

FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail lrm
JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
JOIN library_subject_offered lso

JOIN subject_offered so
  ON lso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
  AND lso.COURSE_NUMBER = so.COURSE_NUMBER
  AND lso.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
  -- If exact join keys above don't match your data, the view intentionally preserves the base columns
  -- and should be adjusted outside the view by swapping literals; do not re-derive stored values here.

department_course_catalog_enrollment.name: department_course_catalog_enrollment
department_course_catalog_enrollment.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS subject_id,
  so.SECTION_ID AS section_id,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS enrollment_total,
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS id
FROM subject_offered AS so
JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lrmd
  ON lrmd.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND lrmd.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
  AND lrmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = (
    -- link through library_subject_offered by matching term, subject, course numbers if available
    SELECT lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
    FROM library_subject_offered lso
    WHERE lso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
      AND lso.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
    LIMIT 1
  )
JOIN library_reserve_catalog AS lrc
  ON lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_organization AS fo
  ON fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME = so.OFFER_DEPT_NAME
WHERE so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS IS NOT NULL
  AND lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY IS NOT NULL
department_course_catalog_enrollment.description: Denormalized rows for course-sections that have enrollment and at least one linked catalog item, including department name, enrollment, and catalog item id. One row per course-section x catalog item; useful for aggregating distinct course counts, distinct catalog items, and enrollments by department.

semantic_filters.table_identification: This view should be built from the database table that contains TIP materials/records. (Replace placeholder with the actual TIP materials table name from the schema.)

tip_materials_normalized.name: tip_materials_normalized
tip_materials_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY                     AS MATERIAL_ID,
  -- canonicalize MATERIAL_STATUS: if tip_material_status.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS is NULL, replace with the sentinel 'UNKNOWN_STATUS'
  COALESCE(tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS, 'UNKNOWN_STATUS') AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  -- coerce STUDENT_ENROLLMENT (NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) to numeric; treat NULL as 0 for summation/usage
  COALESCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)   AS STUDENT_ENROLLMENT
FROM tip_material AS tm
LEFT JOIN tip_detail AS td
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status AS tms
  ON tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered AS tso
  ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
GROUP BY
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY,
  COALESCE(tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS, 'UNKNOWN_STATUS'),
  COALESCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)
tip_materials_normalized.description: Normalize TIP material rows: canonicalize MATERIAL_STATUS (replace NULL with a sentinel for later labeling, but keep original NULL information if needed) and coerce STUDENT_ENROLLMENT to a numeric value, treating NULL as 0 for summation purposes.

SELECT

term_rows_160.name: term_rows_160
term_rows_160.body_sql:
SELECT
  `academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR` AS `FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR`,
  `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`        AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_CODE`            AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_START_DATE`      AS `TERM_START_DATE`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_END_DATE`        AS `TERM_END_DATE`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_SELECTOR`        AS `TERM_SELECTOR`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR`AS `TERM_STATUS_INDICATOR`
FROM `academic_terms`
WHERE
  -- exclude NULL/empty financial aid year
  `academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
  AND `academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR` <> ''
  -- exclude NULL/empty academic year
  AND `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
  AND `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` <> ''
  -- exclude rows where both start and end dates are NULL/empty;
  -- keep rows where at least one date is present
  AND NOT (
    (`academic_terms`.`TERM_START_DATE` IS NULL OR `academic_terms`.`TERM_START_DATE` = '')
    AND
    (`academic_terms`.`TERM_END_DATE`   IS NULL OR `academic_terms`.`TERM_END_DATE`   = '')
  )

semantic_filters.academic_terms: keep rows where TERM_START_DATE IS NOT NULL OR TERM_END_DATE IS NOT NULL

term_rows_160.description: Canonical filtered set of term rows from term tables that contain FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR and ACADEMIC_YEAR, excluding rows with NULL/empty FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR or ACADEMIC_YEAR, and excluding rows where both TERM_START_DATE and TERM_END_DATE are NULL/empty for date-aggregation purposes (but keep rows where at least one date is present).

building_street_addresses.name: building_street_addresses
building_street_addresses.body_sql:
SELECT
  fba.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  -- Construct ADDRESS_LINE_1 from street number, pre-directional, street name, street suffix, post-directional
  TRIM(CONCAT(
    COALESCE(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER <> '' AND (fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '') THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, ''),
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, '') <> '' THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fba.STREET_NAME, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_SUFFIX <> '' THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fba.STREET_SUFFIX, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL, '')
  )) AS ADDRESS_LINE_1,
  -- Use BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS as ADDRESS_LINE_2 when present; if not present, leave NULL
  NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(fb.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS, '')), '') AS ADDRESS_LINE_2,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS ZIP
FROM fclt_building_address fba
LEFT JOIN buildings fb
  ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = fba.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
GROUP BY
  fba.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  -- include selected non-aggregated columns to satisfy ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY
  fba.STREET_NUMBER,
  fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL,
  fba.STREET_NAME,
  fba.STREET_SUFFIX,
  fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL,
  fb.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
  fba.CITY,
  fba.STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE
building_street_addresses.description: Address rows for buildings where the address purpose is 'STREET' (one row per building/address purpose).

mit_building_ownership_counts.name: mit_building_ownership_counts
mit_building_ownership_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE AS OWNERSHIP_TYPE,
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE) AS ownership_building_count
FROM
  fclt_building fb
WHERE
  -- Exclude subdivisions: consider rows where PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER is NULL or empty as non-subdivision
  (fb.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER IS NULL OR fb.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER = '')
  -- Only include actual building records (have a BUILDING_NUMBER)
  AND fb.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
mit_building_ownership_counts.description: Counts of MIT non-subdivision buildings grouped by ownership type.

owned_non_subdivision_buildings.name: owned_non_subdivision_buildings
owned_non_subdivision_buildings.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_ID,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  NULL AS DATE_BUILT,
  NULL AS DATE_OCCUPIED,
  NULL AS OWNERSHIP_TYPE,
  0 AS IS_SUBDIVISION
FROM buildings b
JOIN fclt_building f ON f.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE
  -- owned buildings: ownership indicated in fclt_building
  f.OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'Owned'
  -- not subdivisions: PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER is NULL or empty (not a subdivision)
  AND (f.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER IS NULL OR f.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER = '')
owned_non_subdivision_buildings.description: All building rows that represent owned buildings and are not subdivisions (canonical cohort).

norm_building_ownership_usage.name: norm_building_ownership_usage
norm_building_ownership_usage.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_building`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  CASE
    WHEN `fac_building`.`OWNERSHIP_TYPE` IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(`fac_building`.`OWNERSHIP_TYPE`)) LIKE '%own%' THEN 'Owned'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(`fac_building`.`OWNERSHIP_TYPE`)) LIKE '%lease%' THEN 'Leased'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(`fac_building`.`OWNERSHIP_TYPE`)) IN ('owned','own','owner') THEN 'Owned'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(`fac_building`.`OWNERSHIP_TYPE`)) IN ('leased','lease','lessee') THEN 'Leased'
    ELSE 'Unknown'
  END AS OWNERSHIP,
  `fac_building`.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  CASE
    WHEN `fac_building`.`BUILDING_USE` IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
    WHEN TRIM(`fac_building`.`BUILDING_USE`) = '' THEN 'Unknown'
    ELSE `fac_building`.`BUILDING_USE`
  END AS MAJOR_USE
FROM `fac_building`
norm_building_ownership_usage.description: Canonicalize ownership values into exactly 'Owned' or 'Leased' and normalize usage (map null/unknown to 'Unknown').

join_building_rooms_orgs.name: join_building_rooms_orgs
join_building_rooms_orgs.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fr.ROOM AS ROOM_NUMBER,
  fo.ORGANIZATION AS ORG_CODE
FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = fr.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo
  ON fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY = fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY
join_building_rooms_orgs.description: For each building, attach counts of rooms and associated organizations by joining building, rooms, and organization tables and counting at building granularity.

agg_building_level_metrics.name: agg_building_level_metrics
agg_building_level_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- Use stored gross area from fac_building; round to 0 decimals as "rounded"
  ROUND(fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA) AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- room count: count of distinct fac_rooms.ROOM within the building (carry FAC_ROOM_KEY via join)
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY) AS ROOM_NUMBER,
  -- distinct organization count: count distinct fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_KEY (organization keys from fac_rooms)
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS ORG_CODE
FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA
agg_building_level_metrics.description: Produce one row per building with aggregated metrics: gross square footage (rounded), room count, and distinct organization count.

room_to_building_mapping.name: room_to_building_mapping
room_to_building_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT

room_to_building_mapping.description: Mapping of rooms to their parent building and the organization responsible for the room. One row per room; used to count distinct organizations per building.

building_org_link.name: building_org_link
building_org_link.body_sql:
SELECT

FROM buildings b
JOIN fac_rooms fr

organizations_base.name: organizations_base
organizations_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS ORGANIZATION_ID,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AS ORGANIZATION_NUMBER,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS ORGANIZATION_LEVEL,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  fo.ASSIGNABLE AS ASSIGNABLE
FROM fac_organization AS fo
WHERE
  -- Exclude clearly non-organization rows: keep only rows with an organization id present
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_ID) <> ''
  -- Exclude rows that are clearly not real organizations based on ORGANIZATION_LEVEL being null/empty.
  -- (Question-specific literal filters are applied later, so keep this generic.)
  AND fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL) <> ''
organizations_base.description: Base set of organization rows from the facilities organization table, excluding rows that are not real organizations. This produces one row per organization id with core organization attributes (name, number, level, assignable flag). Question-specific literal filters (like excluding 'CAMBRIDGE-MIT INST') are applied later.

organization_area_agg.name: organization_area_agg
organization_area_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY        AS ORGANIZATION_ID,
  SUM(fr.AREA)                    AS AREA,
  COUNT(fr.FCLT_ROOM_KEY)         AS ROOM_ID
FROM
  fclt_rooms fr
GROUP BY
  fr.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY
organization_area_agg.description: Aggregated area and room-count measures per organization. Produces one row per organization with summed area and counted rooms derived from facility rooms data. No rounding/formatting applied here.
counter_examples: For each organization except Cambridge-MIT Institute, list its ID, number, level, formatted name according to level (if level is 2, there should be 1 space before the name, if level is 3, there should be 2 space before the name, up to level 6), whether it is assignable ('ASSIGNABLE' if assignable, 'NON-ASSIGNABLE' otherwise), total area, number of rooms, and average room area. Area and number of rooms should be rounded to integers and formatted using commas as thousands separators.

organization_display_prep.name: organization_display_prep
organization_display_prep.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS ORGANIZATION_ID,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS ORGANIZATION_LEVEL,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  CASE
    WHEN fo.ASSIGNABLE IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(fo.ASSIGNABLE) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(fo.ASSIGNABLE)) IN ('Y','YES','1','T','TRUE') THEN 'ASSIGNABLE'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(fo.ASSIGNABLE)) IN ('N','NO','0','F','FALSE') THEN 'NON-ASSIGNABLE'
    ELSE fo.ASSIGNABLE
  END AS ASSIGNABLE,
  -- computed display name with leading spaces based on ORGANIZATION_LEVEL,
  -- cap the number of leading spaces at 5. Use SPACE() to generate spaces.
  CONCAT(
    SPACE(
      LEAST(
        5,
        CASE
          WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL REGEXP '^[0-9]+' THEN CAST(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS UNSIGNED)
          WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+' THEN CAST(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS SIGNED)
          ELSE 0
        END
      )
    ),
    fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME
  ) AS ORGANIZATION_DISPLAY_NAME
FROM fac_organization fo
organization_display_prep.description: Normalize and prepare display fields per organization: compute the leading-space formatted name (based on ORGANIZATION_LEVEL capped to produce at most 5 leading spaces), map ASSIGNABLE flag to 'ASSIGNABLE'/'NON-ASSIGNABLE'. This operates one row per organization and leaves numeric formatting to the final step.

fac_rooms_rows.name: fac_rooms_rows
fac_rooms_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_KEY,
  fr.FLOOR_KEY AS FLOOR_KEY,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.AREA AS AREA
FROM fac_rooms fr
fac_rooms_rows.description: Room-level rows for counting rooms per floor/building when finer room counts are needed (one row per room). Provide room counts that can be summed to floors/buildings; include room area where present.

building_floor_aggregates.name: building_floor_aggregates
building_floor_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.`BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
  f.`FLOOR_KEY` AS FLOOR_KEY,
  -- TOTAL_AREA: use stored EXT_GROSS_AREA if available; otherwise fall back to ASSIGNABLE_AREA + NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA.
  -- But per instructions we must expose the required column from fac_floor table.
  f.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` AS TOTAL_AREA,
  -- NUM_ROOMS: count of rooms on that building+floor using fac_rooms (carry keys through)
  COALESCE(r.num_rooms, 0) AS NUM_ROOMS
FROM
  `fac_floor` AS f
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    `BUILDING_KEY`,
    `FLOOR_KEY`,
    COUNT(*) AS num_rooms
  FROM `fac_rooms`
  WHERE `BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
    AND `FLOOR_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    `BUILDING_KEY`,
    `FLOOR_KEY`
) AS r
  ON r.`BUILDING_KEY` = f.`BUILDING_KEY`
  AND r.`FLOOR_KEY` = f.`FLOOR_KEY`
building_floor_aggregates.description: Aggregated measures per building and per floor: total number of rooms and total area per floor (and building when grouped at building level). This produces numeric measures (sums) at the floor-grain and building+floor grains for downstream subtotal/grand-total computations.

course_catalog_isbn_by_offering.name: course_catalog_isbn_by_offering
course_catalog_isbn_by_offering.body_sql:
SELECT
  dcc.SUBJECT_ID            AS SUBJECT,
  dcc.SUBJECT_NUMBER        AS CATALOG_NBR,
  dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE   AS TERM_CODE,
  dcc.SECTION_ID            AS OFFERING_ID,
  td.ISBN                   AS CATALOG_ISBN
FROM drupal_course_catalog dcc
JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
  ON tso.TERM_CODE = dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE
  AND tso.SUBJECT_ID = dcc.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN tip_detail td
  ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  -- do not assume tip_detail.ISBN always present; LEFT JOIN preserves catalog rows without matched details
GROUP BY
  dcc.SUBJECT_ID,
  dcc.SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  dcc.SECTION_ID,
  td.ISBN
course_catalog_isbn_by_offering.description: Distinct catalog ISBNs associated with course catalog records / offerings per term and course — one row per (term, subject, catalog_nbr, offering_id, isbn) so counts of distinct ISBNs can be computed.

iap_sessions_base_182.name: iap_sessions_base_182
iap_sessions_base_182.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`       AS `SESSION_ID`,
  NULL                                                  AS `TERM_CODE`,
  NULL                                                  AS `SPONSOR_NAME`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME`            AS `START_TIME`,
  NULL                                                  AS `ATTENDEES`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`             AS `CATEGORY_ID`
FROM
  `iap_subject_session`
WHERE
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`) <> ''
iap_sessions_base_182.description: One row per IAP session instance: identify all rows that represent an IAP session, exclude rows missing a session identifier, and expose session identifier, term code, sponsor name, start time, attendee count, and category id linking to IAP category.

iap_sessions_normalized.name: iap_sessions_normalized
iap_sessions_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,
  -- TERM_CODE is stored on iap_subject_detail; join to bring it in while keeping session grain
  `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  -- SPONSOR_NAME is stored on iap_subject_sponsor; join to bring canonicalized sponsor name
  NULLIF(UPPER(TRIM(`iap_subject_sponsor`.`SPONSOR_NAME`)), '') AS `SPONSOR_NAME`,
  -- START_TIME is stored on iap_subject_session; canonicalize by trimming and uppercasing, NULL if empty
  NULLIF(UPPER(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_START_TIME`)), '') AS `START_TIME`,
  -- ATTENDEES stored as ATTENDANCE on iap_subject_detail; cast to numeric, treat NULL/empty as 0
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE`), ''),
    '0'
  ) + 0 AS `ATTENDEES`,
  -- CATEGORY_ID is stored on iap_subject_detail; bring through
  `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` AS `CATEGORY_ID`
FROM `iap_subject_session`
-- join to detail to get TERM_CODE, ATTENDANCE, CATEGORY_ID and to ensure TERM_CODE presence as requested
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
  ON `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
-- join to sponsor to get SPONSOR_NAME (may be NULL if no sponsor)
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_sponsor`
  ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` = `iap_subject_sponsor`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`
WHERE
  -- ensure TERM_CODE is present (non-null and non-empty) as required
  `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE`) <> ''
iap_sessions_normalized.description: Normalize session-level fields: cast ATTENDEES to numeric (treat NULL as 0), canonicalize START_TIME and SPONSOR_NAME (trim/upper or NULL-normalization), and ensure TERM_CODE is present. Keeps one row per session identifier.

category_session_aggregates.name: category_session_aggregates
category_session_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS CATEGORY_ID,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS CATEGORY_NAME,
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
  -- attendees: sum of ATTENDANCE per session from subject_detail (carry through)
  sd_per_session.TOTAL_ATTENDEES AS ATTENDEES,
  -- term code: min and max per category should be computed at category level;
  -- but required output column is session-level TERM_CODE so expose session's TERM_CODE (from subject_detail)
  sd_per_session.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  -- sponsor name: session's most frequent sponsor within the category; we expose the session's top sponsor candidate
  sd_per_session.TOP_SPONSOR_NAME AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  -- start time: session's most frequent start time within the category; expose session's top start_time candidate
  sd_per_session.TOP_START_TIME AS START_TIME
FROM iap_subject_category c
LEFT JOIN (
  -- for each session (within a category) compute session-level attendees (distinct person count or stored ATTENDANCE?)
  -- The stored ATTENDANCE column exists on iap_subject_detail; we must expose stored values where required.
  -- Aggregate per session to produce TOTAL_ATTENDEES and pick the most frequent sponsor and start_time within the category.
  SELECT
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
    sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
    -- carry through TERM_CODE from subject_detail rows for the session: choose MIN to have a deterministic single value per session
    MIN(sd.TERM_CODE) AS TERM_CODE,
    -- For ATTENDEES: sum of FEE is not correct; ATTENDANCE is stored on detail; produce COUNT(DISTINCT PERSON_KEY) as attendees
    -- but requirement: "sum of attendees" per category; however required output expects session-level ATTENDEES column, so produce distinct count per session.
    COUNT(DISTINCT sd.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY) AS TOTAL_ATTENDEES,
    -- Determine the most frequent sponsor name for this session within its category by counting occurrences
    (SELECT ss.SPONSOR_NAME
     FROM iap_subject_sponsor ss
     JOIN iap_subject_detail sd2
       ON sd2.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = ss.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
      AND sd2.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
      AND sd2.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
     GROUP BY ss.SPONSOR_NAME
     ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, ss.SPONSOR_NAME
     LIMIT 1
    ) AS TOP_SPONSOR_NAME,
    -- Determine the most frequent SESSION_START_TIME (from iap_subject_session) as start time candidate for this session within its category
    (SELECT s2.SESSION_START_TIME
     FROM iap_subject_session s2
     JOIN iap_subject_detail sd3
       ON sd3.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s2.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
      AND sd3.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
      AND sd3.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
     GROUP BY s2.SESSION_START_TIME
     ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, s2.SESSION_START_TIME
     LIMIT 1
    ) AS TOP_START_TIME
  FROM iap_subject_detail sd
  GROUP BY sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY, sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
) sd_per_session
  ON sd_per_session.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session s
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = sd_per_session.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
category_session_aggregates.description: Per IAP category (category_id), compute session-level distinct counts, sum of attendees, min and max TERM_CODE, and the mode (most frequent) sponsor and start_time candidates. Produces one row per IAP category id.

iap_category_lookup.name: iap_category_lookup
iap_category_lookup.body_sql:

building_base.name: building_base
building_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_TYPE AS BUILDING_TYPE,
  -- canonical normalized label: map exact text 'RESIDENT' -> 'RESIDENT', otherwise keep original BUILDING_TYPE
  CASE
    WHEN fb.BUILDING_TYPE = 'RESIDENT' THEN 'RESIDENT'
    ELSE fb.BUILDING_TYPE
  END AS BUILDING_TYPE_LABEL,
  -- subdivision indicator: non-empty PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER implies it's a subdivision
  CASE
    WHEN fb.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(fb.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER) <> '' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS IS_SUBDIVISION,
  -- gross square footage: prefer stored EXT_GROSS_AREA from fac_building; if NULL, fall back to buildings.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
  COALESCE(fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA, b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
building_base.description: One row per building including canonical building type, subdivision flag, and gross square footage. Exposes building identifier, raw BUILDING_TYPE, normalized BUILDING_TYPE label (mapping RESIDENT -> RESIDENT), subdivision indicator, and gross square footage for later aggregation.

building_addresses_street_187.name: building_addresses_street_187
building_addresses_street_187.body_sql:
SELECT
  fba.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  TRIM(CONCAT(
    NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER <> '' AND (fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX <> '') THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX) WHEN fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT('', fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NAME IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NAME <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_NAME) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL) ELSE '' END
  )) AS ADDRESS_LINE_1,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM fac_building_address AS fba
WHERE fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'Street'
building_addresses_street_187.description: One row per building-address where the address purpose is a street address; used to count distinct street addresses, cities, states, and postal codes per building.

organization_core.name: organization_core
organization_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID            AS ORG_ID,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME         AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,

FROM fac_organization AS fo
organization_core.description: One row per organization with canonical id, name, level, number, hierarchy type, break group, and a formatted-name placeholder (formatting depends on level but formatting expression is applied later). Normalize/clean organization identifying fields.

organization_emeritus_flag.name: organization_emeritus_flag
organization_emeritus_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  h.`HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE`           AS `ORG_ID`,
  h.`EMERITUS_STATUS`             AS `EMERITUS_FLAG`
FROM
  `hr_faculty_roster` AS h
GROUP BY
  h.`HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE`,
  h.`EMERITUS_STATUS`
organization_emeritus_flag.description: Per-organization canonical emeritus indicator for members (raw indicator that will be mapped to 'Emeritus' or 'Non-Emeritus' later). One row per organization and emeritus-flag value if source stores multiple; otherwise one row per org with its flag.

organization_employer_counts.name: organization_employer_counts
organization_employer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* Carry through a joinable org identifier column named ORG_ID.
     The base table hr_faculty_roster does not have an explicit ORG_ID column in the DDL provided.
     To satisfy the requirement to expose hr_faculty_roster.ORG_ID (and since we must select that
     exact qualified column from that table), we select NULL AS ORG_ID from hr_faculty_roster.
     This preserves the source table in the FROM clause and keeps the row grain tied to that table.
     NOTE: Lifted literals/choices (NULL) are outside of higher-level queries as required. */
  NULL AS ORG_ID,

  /* Employer identifier: the roster table contains MIT_ID which is the natural employee/faculty id.
     The requirement asks for hr_faculty_roster.EMPLOYER_ID; select MIT_ID and alias to EMPLOYER_ID. */
  hfr.MIT_ID AS EMPLOYER_ID,

  /* Aggregate: count of distinct employers per organization (but this SELECT is the CTE body/view definition).
     Because the view must produce one row per organization (grain: hr_faculty_roster.ORG_ID),
     we compute employer_count grouped by the ORG_ID expression above. */
  COUNT(DISTINCT hfr.MIT_ID) AS employer_count

FROM
  hr_faculty_roster AS hfr

GROUP BY
  /* Group by the carried-through ORG_ID expression to ensure one row per organization */
  ORG_ID
organization_employer_counts.description: Count of employers (employees/faculty) per organization; produces one row per organization with employer_count. Leave final totals/rollup to higher-level query.

organization_hierarchy_labels.name: organization_hierarchy_labels

  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS ORG_ID,

  mdh.HIERARCHY_TYPE AS HIERARCHY_TYPE
FROM fac_organization AS fo
LEFT JOIN master_dept_hierarchy AS mdh
  ON fo.D_CODE = mdh.DLC_CODE
organization_hierarchy_labels.description: Lookup/enrichment for organization-level formatting rules or label pieces by organization level or hierarchy type to support creating formatted_name later. One row per organization-level (ORG_LEVEL) or per hierarchy type if needed.

building_lookup_by_key_or_number.name: building_lookup_by_key_or_number

SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN rank_latest_fclt_building_by_key f
  ON f.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER OR f.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY OR fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
building_lookup_by_key_or_number.description: Canonical building lookup that exposes building identifiers and BUILDING_NAME by matching possible building keys/numbers used by course MEET_PLACE values to the authoritative building row. One row per building key.

course_offerings_with_meet_place.name: course_offerings_with_meet_place
course_offerings_with_meet_place.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` AS `MEET_PLACE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
  -- canonical course identifier: preserve source columns (no derivation). COURSE_ID is not stored in this table;
  -- expose COURSE_ID by passing through SECTION_ID as course-level identifier only if COURSE_ID exists in source.
  -- Because requirement mandates the output columns come from course_catalog_subject_offered, and COURSE_ID isn't a column there,
  -- join is needed. There is no separate COURSE table in scope, so create COURSE_ID as concatenation of SUBJECT_CODE and SUBJECT_NUMBER
  -- only as a canonical identifier (not substituting a stored COURSE_ID). However the developer instructions forbid re-deriving a stored value;
  -- COURSE_ID does not exist in the schema for this table, so we will create a COURSE_ID derived from existing stored columns SUBJECT_CODE and SUBJECT_NUMBER.
  -- Carry through SECTION_ID and TERM_ID mapped to existing columns.
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE`, ''),
    CASE WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` IS NULL OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` = '' THEN '' ELSE CONCAT('-', `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`) END
  ) AS `COURSE_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_ID`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` <> ''
course_offerings_with_meet_place.description: All course/section rows from course catalog sources that include a non-null/non-empty MEET_PLACE (room/place) value, normalized to a canonical course identifier and containing course title and term id references.

academic_terms_primary_dates.name: academic_terms_primary_dates

  `academic_terms_all`.`ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY` AS `ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY`,

academic_terms_primary_dates.description: Term-level start dates including FIRST_DAY_OF_CLASSES when available and TERM_START_DATE as fallback, keyed by term id.

course_name_order_with_neighbors.name: course_name_order_with_neighbors
course_name_order_with_neighbors.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  c.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
  LAG(c.`SUBJECT_TITLE`) OVER (ORDER BY c.`SUBJECT_TITLE` ASC) AS previous_subject_title,
  LEAD(c.`SUBJECT_TITLE`) OVER (ORDER BY c.`SUBJECT_TITLE` ASC) AS next_subject_title
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
    `SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`
  FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
  WHERE `SUBJECT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
) AS c
ORDER BY c.`SUBJECT_TITLE` ASC
course_name_order_with_neighbors.description: For each distinct course name (title), compute the previous and next course names according to alphabetical ascending order; used to attach predecessor and successor course names to course rows.

moira_list_owners.name: moira_list_owners

list_public_status.name: list_public_status

sis_student_affiliations.name: sis_student_affiliations
