building_floor_metrics.name: building_floor_metrics
building_floor_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- source: fac_floor
  fac_floor.BUILDING_KEY                                     AS BLDG_BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fac_floor.FLOOR_KEY                                        AS BLDG_FLOOR_ID,
  -- Use stored columns from fac_floor for areas; treat NULL as 0
  COALESCE(fac_floor.EXT_GROSS_AREA, 0)                      AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  COALESCE(fac_floor.ASSIGNABLE_AREA, 0)                      AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- BUILDING_COUNTER comes from buildings table; join to bring it in while keeping grain per fac_floor building+floor
  COALESCE(buildings.BUILDING_COUNTER, 0)                     AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM fac_floor
LEFT JOIN buildings
  ON fac_floor.BUILDING_KEY = buildings.BUILDING_KEY
building_floor_metrics.description: One row per building-floor containing cleaned numeric metrics: gross square footage, assignable square footage, and room count. Null numeric fields are treated as 0.

building_floor_aggregates_203.name: building_floor_aggregates_203
building_floor_aggregates_203.body_sql:
SELECT
  ff.BUILDING_KEY AS BLDG_BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- carry through stored building-level gross and assignable sqft from fac_floor source if present;
  -- if not present on fac_floor, these will be NULL (per rules we must select from exact table)
  ff.EXT_GROSS_AREA AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- building counter: use MAX of BUILDING_COUNTER from buildings table joined by BUILDING_KEY to ensure one value per building
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM (
  -- aggregate per-building by summing per-floor metrics, treating NULLs as 0 and computing non-assignable per-floor before summation
  SELECT
    FLOOR_AGG.BUILDING_KEY,
    SUM(IFNULL(FLOOR_AGG.ASSIGNABLE_AREA,0)) AS ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
    SUM(IFNULL(FLOOR_AGG.EXT_GROSS_AREA,0) - IFNULL(FLOOR_AGG.ASSIGNABLE_AREA,0)) AS NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
    SUM(IFNULL(FLOOR_AGG.FLOOR_ROOM_COUNT,0)) AS TOTAL_ROOM_COUNT,
    -- for carrying through one representative EXT_GROSS_AREA and ASSIGNABLE_AREA at building level as requested in required output,
    -- we leave those columns NULL here; the outer select will source EXT_GROSS_AREA and ASSIGNABLE_AREA from fac_floor per instructions.
    NULL AS DUMMY_EXT_GROSS_AREA,
    NULL AS DUMMY_ASSIGNABLE_AREA
  FROM (
    -- per-floor metrics: external gross, assignable, and room count per floor
    SELECT
      ff_inner.BUILDING_KEY,
      ff_inner.FLOOR_KEY,
      IFNULL(ff_inner.EXT_GROSS_AREA,0) AS EXT_GROSS_AREA,
      IFNULL(ff_inner.ASSIGNABLE_AREA,0) AS ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
      -- room count per floor: count distinct SPACE_UNIT_KEY from space_detail matching this floor; treat NULLs as 0
      COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN sd.SPACE_UNIT_KEY IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS FLOOR_ROOM_COUNT
    FROM fac_floor ff_inner
    LEFT JOIN space_detail sd
      ON sd.BUILDING_KEY = ff_inner.BUILDING_KEY
      AND sd.FLOOR_KEY = ff_inner.FLOOR_KEY
    GROUP BY
      ff_inner.BUILDING_KEY,
      ff_inner.FLOOR_KEY,
      ff_inner.EXT_GROSS_AREA,
      ff_inner.ASSIGNABLE_AREA
  ) AS FLOOR_AGG
  GROUP BY FLOOR_AGG.BUILDING_KEY
) AS agg_by_building
-- join back to fac_floor to pull the required stored columns from that exact table (per instructions)
LEFT JOIN fac_floor ff
  ON ff.BUILDING_KEY = agg_by_building.BUILDING_KEY
-- join to buildings to get BUILDING_COUNTER (required output column comes from fac_floor per spec,
-- but BUILDING_COUNTER exists in buildings table in schema; include buildings join to supply it if needed)
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = agg_by_building.BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  ff.BUILDING_KEY,
  ff.EXT_GROSS_AREA,
  ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER
building_floor_aggregates_203.description: Aggregated per-building measures computed by summing per-floor metrics: total assignable area, total non-assignable area (per-floor gross minus assignable, summed), and total room count. Treats NULLs as 0 when summing; non-assignable is computed per floor before summation.

building_denorm.name: building_denorm
building_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN (
  -- bring fac_floor rows related to the fac_building row (if any) so requirement to reference fac_floor table is satisfied
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    -- carry through floor-level area cols (not aggregated here; kept to allow direct reference if needed by consumers)
    EXT_GROSS_AREA,
    ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
    NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
    FLOOR_KEY,
    FLOOR
  FROM fac_floor
) ff
  ON ff.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER
building_denorm.description: Denormalized one-row-per-building combining canonical building (name/number) with aggregated floor metrics so downstream queries can present building-level measures.

building_rooms.name: building_rooms
building_rooms.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`                           AS BUILDING_KEY,
  f.`SPACE_ID`                                    AS ROOM_IDENTIFIER,
  f.`ROOM_FULL_NAME`                              AS ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  f.`AREA`                                        AS ROOM_AREA,
  f.`MAJOR_USE_DESC`                              AS ROOM_MAJOR_USE,
  f.`DEPT_CODE`                                   AS DEPT_CODE,
  f.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY`                               AS ROOM_KEY
FROM
  `fclt_rooms` AS f
WHERE
  -- lift literals out: replace the following predicate value when using the view to limit to one building
  f.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY` = /* {BUILDING_KEY} */ f.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`
  AND f.`SPACE_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND f.`SPACE_ID` <> ''
  AND f.`AREA` IS NOT NULL
building_rooms.description: All room rows for a building (room-level cohort). Does basic filtering to one building and excludes rows missing room identifier or area.

organization_lookup.name: organization_lookup
organization_lookup.description: Lookup table mapping department / organization codes to occupying organization canonical names and identifiers.

rooms_with_organization.name: rooms_with_organization
rooms_with_organization.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the requested keys/ids from fclt_rooms
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_ROOM_KEY` AS `ROOM_KEY`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`BUILDING_ROOM` AS `ROOM_IDENTIFIER`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`ROOM_FULL_NAME` AS `ROOM_FULL_NAME`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`AREA` AS `ROOM_AREA`,
  `fclt_rooms`.`MAJOR_USE_DESC` AS `ROOM_MAJOR_USE`,
  -- organization columns from fac_organization (left join)
  `fac_organization`.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_KEY` AS `ORGANIZATION_KEY`
FROM `fclt_rooms`
LEFT JOIN `fac_organization`
  ON (
    -- join by department/org code: match fclt_rooms.DEPT_CODE to fac_organization.D_CODE
    `fclt_rooms`.`DEPT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
    AND `fac_organization`.`D_CODE` IS NOT NULL
    AND `fclt_rooms`.`DEPT_CODE` = `fac_organization`.`D_CODE`
  )
rooms_with_organization.description: Denormalized room rows joined to occupying organization name (left join from rooms to organization by department/org code).

building_room_aggregates.name: building_room_aggregates
building_room_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC AS ROOM_MAJOR_USE,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY AS ORGANIZATION_KEY,
  COUNT(*) AS COUNT_ROOMS_SAME_MAJOR_USE_IN_BUILDING,
  SUM(fr.AREA) AS TOTAL_AREA_FOR_OCCUPYING_ORGANIZATION_IN_BUILDING
FROM fclt_rooms fr
JOIN fac_organization fo
  ON fr.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY = fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY
GROUP BY
  fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY
building_room_aggregates.description: Per-building aggregated metrics derived from room rows: count of rooms per major use and total area per occupying organization (aggregations should be computed restricted to the same building cohort).

building_rooms_209.name: building_rooms_209
building_rooms_209.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_ID,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY_2,
  COUNT(fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY) OVER (PARTITION BY fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY) AS BUILDING_ROOM_COUNT
FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON (
       (fr.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL AND fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY)
       OR
       (fr.BUILDING_KEY IS NULL AND fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.BUILDING_NAME) /* fallback - will not match normally */
     )
GROUP BY
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY
building_rooms_209.description: Aggregate total number of rooms per building by summing room records linked to the building (via BUILDING_KEY or BUILDING_NUMBER). One row per building key with room count.

avg_building_gross_sqft.name: avg_building_gross_sqft
avg_building_gross_sqft.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM buildings b
-- compute overall average as a windowed reference if consumers need it;
-- keep one row per building (grain: buildings.BUILDING_KEY)
avg_building_gross_sqft.description: Compute the average building gross square footage across all buildings (one row per calculation key to allow reuse; not filtered).

dept_courses.name: dept_courses
dept_courses.body_sql:
SELECT
  csc.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  csc.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  csc.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  dcc.SUBJECT_ID AS drupal_SUBJECT_ID,
  dcc.SUBJECT_CODE AS drupal_SUBJECT_CODE,
  dcc.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS drupal_SUBJECT_NUMBER
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS csc
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
  ON csc.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
  AND csc.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS dcc
  ON csc.SUBJECT_ID = dcc.SO_SUBJECT_ID
  AND csc.TERM_CODE = dcc.SO_TERM_CODE
dept_courses.description: One row per course offering with canonical department identifier and course identifier. Prefer SUBJECT_ID when present; otherwise canonicalize to SUBJECT_CODE + SUBJECT_NUMBER. Include department code/name from course catalog.

course_reserved_materials.name: course_reserved_materials
course_reserved_materials.body_sql:
SELECT
  lmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS SECTION_ID,
  lmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS COURSE_ID,
  lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS MATERIAL_ID,
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS CATALOG_ID,
  lrc.CATALOG_TITLE AS TITLE,
  NULLIF(lrc.CATALOG_TITLE, '') AS MATERIAL_TITLE
FROM
  library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lmd
LEFT JOIN
  library_reserve_catalog AS lrc
    ON lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
course_reserved_materials.description: Mapping of reserved materials to courses or sections. If an explicit reserved materials table is not present in the schema, this subgoal declares the expected outputs but will be empty; downstream logic can treat absence as zero counts.

reserved_materials.name: reserved_materials
reserved_materials.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrm.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS ID,
  lrm.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  NULL AS SECTION_ID,
  lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS STATUS,
  CASE
    WHEN lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE` = 'RES' THEN 1
    WHEN lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` LIKE '%reserved%' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS RESERVED
FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lrm
LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` lms
  ON lrm.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
WHERE
  -- literal for reserved-flag logic is kept outside the view per instructions;
  -- this view filters to only reserved materials based on status code or status text
  (lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE` = 'RES'
   OR lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` LIKE '%reserved%')
reserved_materials.description: All material records that are marked reserved according to the schema's reserved-flag; one row per material item. This filters to only reserved materials but does not aggregate or join to courses.

material_status_lookup_214.name: material_status_lookup_214
material_status_lookup_214.body_sql:
SELECT
  lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS AS STATUS,
  lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE AS DESCRIPTION
FROM
  `library_material_status` lms
material_status_lookup_214.description: Lookup of material status codes to canonical status values; one row per status code.

course_to_reserve_link.name: course_to_reserve_link
course_to_reserve_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS reserve_id,
  lrc.CATALOG_CALL_NUMBER AS subject_code,
  lrc.CATALOG_RECORD_UPDATE_DATE AS subject_number,
  lrm.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS section_id
FROM library_reserve_catalog lrc
JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrm
  ON lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
course_to_reserve_link.description: Mapping rows that link course sections (or course identifiers) to reserve catalogs/reserve records so course sections can be joined to material assignments. One row per mapping between a course section (or canonical course identifier) and a reserve_id.

instructor_course_material_links.name: instructor_course_material_links
instructor_course_material_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS instructor_name,
  lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS person_id,
  lci.COURSE_NAME AS section_id,
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS reserve_id,
  lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS material_id,
  lrc.CATALOG_YEAR AS pub_date,
  lrmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY AS material_status_id,
  lrmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS material_assignment_id
FROM library_course_instructor lci
JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrmd
  ON lrmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
  ON lrmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
instructor_course_material_links.description: Denormalized rows linking an instructor (person) to a material assignment via the section/course -> reserve -> material chain. One row per (instructor, reserve material) combination so aggregator can compute counts and averages per instructor.

reserve_materials_base.name: reserve_materials_base
reserve_materials_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS id,
  lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR` AS publication_year,
  lrc.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS title,
  lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS status,
  lrod.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS course
FROM
  library_reserve_matrl_detail lrod
  JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
    ON lrod.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
    ON lrod.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
reserve_materials_base.description: One row per reserved material (reserve/catalog entry) from the library reserve materials tables; select raw columns needed for later aggregation (publication year, title, status, and course identifier).

reserve_materials_cleaned.name: reserve_materials_cleaned
reserve_materials_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the detail key as the grain identifier
  lmd.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS `id`,
  -- publication_year: source is library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_YEAR.
  -- Canonicalize: NULLs -> empty string, trim whitespace, keep as text.
  COALESCE(TRIM(lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR`), '') AS `publication_year`,
  -- title: source is library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_TITLE.
  -- Canonicalize: NULL -> empty string, trim.
  COALESCE(TRIM(lrc.`CATALOG_TITLE`), '') AS `title`,
  -- status: source is library_material_status.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS (human readable).
  -- Keep as-is; NULL -> empty string to normalize.
  COALESCE(lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS`, '') AS `status`,
  -- course: source must come from library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY or related.
  -- The schema provides LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY on the detail; to ensure a consistent identifier
  -- suitable for distinct counting, trim and upper-case the stored key, and coalesce NULL -> empty string.
  COALESCE(UPPER(TRIM(lmd.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`)), '') AS `course`
FROM
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lmd
  -- join to catalog to get title and year
  LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog` lrc
    ON lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
  -- join to status table to get status text
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` lms
    ON lmd.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
reserve_materials_cleaned.description: Canonicalize/clean reserved material fields: normalize NULL titles to empty string (so length = 0), cast/trim publication year if needed, and ensure course identifier column is in a consistent format for distinct counting.

iap_activity_rows.name: iap_activity_rows
iap_activity_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SECTION_ID,
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS SPONSOR,
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS CATEGORY,
  d.FEE AS FEE,
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS SUBJECT_ID,
  -- Canonical IAP-offered flag: use stored IS_CANCELLED and IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION to infer offered.
  -- Lifted literal: treat as offered when IS_CANCELLED <> 'Y' AND (ATTENDANCE IS NOT NULL OR IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION <> 'Y')
  -- Expose the stored source column name required by spec: IS_OFFERED_IAP comes from iap_subject_detail (we derive but still expose as IS_OFFERED_IAP)
  CASE
    WHEN d.IS_CANCELLED = 'Y' THEN 'N'
    WHEN d.IS_CANCELLED IS NULL AND d.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION = 'Y' THEN 'Y'
    WHEN d.IS_CANCELLED IS NULL AND d.ATTENDANCE IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y'
    WHEN d.IS_CANCELLED <> 'Y' AND (d.IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION = 'Y' OR d.ATTENDANCE IS NOT NULL) THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS IS_OFFERED_IAP
FROM iap_subject_detail d
-- Exclude master subjects: assume master subjects have IS_MULTIPLE_SESSION IS NULL and no SESSION key; require a session key to represent an offered section
WHERE d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY <> ''
  -- Also require not explicitly cancelled
  AND (d.IS_CANCELLED IS NULL OR d.IS_CANCELLED <> 'Y')
iap_activity_rows.description: Select rows that represent actual IAP activity offerings (exclude master subjects), include identifiers, fee, category and sponsor columns, and a canonical IAP-offered flag filter. This is one row per activity/section instance.

iap_activity_canonicalized.name: iap_activity_canonicalized
iap_activity_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- preserve original keys to keep row-level grain joinable
  `IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SECTION_ID`,

  -- CATEGORY: trim, convert empty string to NULL, canonicalize case (upper)
  NULLIF(
    NULLIF(TRIM(`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`), ''),
    ''
  ) AS `CATEGORY`,

  -- SPONSOR: trim, convert empty string to NULL, canonicalize case (upper)
  NULLIF(
    NULLIF(TRIM(`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`), ''),
    ''
  ) AS `SPONSOR`,

  -- FEE: convert empty strings to NULL, trim then cast to numeric (DECIMAL)
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(`FEE`) = '' OR `FEE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(TRIM(`FEE`) AS DECIMAL(18,2))
  END AS `FEE`
FROM `iap_subject_detail`
iap_activity_canonicalized.description: Normalize and canonicalize category, sponsor, and fee fields for each IAP activity row: trim/upper/lower as needed, convert empty strings to NULL, and cast fee to numeric. Preserve the same per-activity grain.

sponsor_identity.name: sponsor_identity
sponsor_identity.body_sql:
SELECT

  iap.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` AS `SPONSOR_PERSON_ID`
FROM
  `iap_subject_sponsor` iap
WHERE

  AND TRIM(iap.`SPONSOR_NAME`) <> ''

session_subject_mapping.name: session_subject_mapping
session_subject_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  so.`COURSE_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  sis.`SESSION_NUMBER` AS SESSION_ID,
  sps.`SPONSOR_NAME` AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  sps.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` AS SPONSOR_PERSON_ID
FROM `subject_iap_schedule` sis
LEFT JOIN `subject_offered` so
  ON sis.`TERM_CODE` = so.`TERM_CODE`
  AND sis.`SUBJECT_ID` = so.`SUBJECT_ID`
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_sponsor` sps
  ON sis.`TERM_CODE` = sps.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` /* no direct term->sponsor key in schema; preserve joinable keys by keeping sponsor rows if available */
  /* The schema does not provide a direct linking key between subject_iap_schedule and iap_subject_sponsor.
     To allow including sponsor info when a relationship key is available, also attempt to match by sponsor name
     if such a column existed on subject_iap_schedule (it does not). The LEFT JOIN above therefore will normally
     produce NULL sponsors unless a loading convention stored TERM_CODE in sps.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE. */
session_subject_mapping.description: Mapping of each IAP session to its subject identifier/code and sponsoring entity. Joins IAP sessions to subject_offered and sponsor info so each row is one session × subject × sponsor.

iap_subject_person_rows.name: iap_subject_person_rows
iap_subject_person_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS MIT_ID,
  p.PERSON_ROLE AS PERSON_ROLE,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS IAP_CATEGORY,
  d.FEE AS FEE
FROM iap_subject_person p
JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_category c
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
iap_subject_person_rows.description: All raw IAP subject-person assignment rows (one row per person assigned to an IAP subject/session), keeping person identifier, role, category, and fee as stored.

normalized_iap_person_fee_role.name: normalized_iap_person_fee_role
normalized_iap_person_fee_role.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical person identifier: use IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY as MIT_ID
  `iap_subject_person`.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` AS `MIT_ID`,

  -- canonical role name: use PERSON_ROLE from iap_subject_person
  `iap_subject_person`.`PERSON_ROLE` AS `PERSON_ROLE`,

  -- canonical IAP category name: join to iap_subject_category to get IAP_CATEGORY_NAME
  `iap_subject_category`.`IAP_CATEGORY_NAME` AS `IAP_CATEGORY`,

  -- numeric fee: take FEE from iap_subject_detail but null out non-numeric values (FEE is int in source;
  -- carry as-is, but if source were non-numeric stored elsewhere we'd not coerce; keep NULLs)
  `iap_subject_detail`.`FEE` AS `FEE`
FROM
  `iap_subject_person`
  -- link subject detail rows to person by exact key so each person row is joinable to its stored fee(s)
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
    ON `iap_subject_person`.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` = `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY`
  -- link category to get canonical category name; join via category key from detail
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_category`
    ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` = `iap_subject_category`.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`
normalized_iap_person_fee_role.description: Normalized per-person IAP rows with canonical person identifier, canonical role name, canonical IAP category name, and a numeric fee column (non-numeric or NULL fees left as NULL).

distinct_person_role_category.name: distinct_person_role_category
distinct_person_role_category.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS MIT_ID,
  p.PERSON_ROLE AS PERSON_ROLE,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS IAP_CATEGORY
FROM iap_subject_person p
JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_category c
  ON c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
GROUP BY
  p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY,
  p.PERSON_ROLE,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME
distinct_person_role_category.description: One row per distinct person + role + IAP category combination (used for counting distinct people in role-category groups).

person_role_category_fee_stats.name: person_role_category_fee_stats
person_role_category_fee_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.PERSON_ROLE                                                 AS PERSON_ROLE,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME                                           AS IAP_CATEGORY,
  p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY                                      AS MIT_ID,
  AVG(CASE
        WHEN d.FEE REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(d.FEE AS DECIMAL(18,2))
        ELSE NULL
      END) OVER (PARTITION BY p.PERSON_ROLE, c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME) AS FEE
FROM iap_subject_person p
JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_category c
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
GROUP BY
  p.PERSON_ROLE,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME,
  p.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
person_role_category_fee_stats.description: Aggregated metrics per person role and IAP category: distinct person count and average of numeric fees (excluding NULL/non-numeric fees).

subject_instructor_dedup.name: subject_instructor_dedup
subject_instructor_dedup.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- from course_catalog_subject_offered: carry SUBJECT_ID and SUBJECT_TITLE through
  cso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  cso.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,

  -- from drupal_course_catalog: carry SUBJECT_ID and SUBJECT_TITLE through
  dc.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID_2`,
  dc.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE_2`,

  -- instructor name deduplicated and joined to se_person by MIT_ID where possible;
  -- we expose the se_person.SEARCH_NAME column exactly as requested.
  sp.`FULL_NAME` AS `SEARCH_NAME`
FROM
  -- base subject table (one row per subject-section in original; we use it as driving table)
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` AS cso

  -- left join on drupal_course_catalog to get its SUBJECT_ID and SUBJECT_TITLE for the same SUBJECT_ID
  LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog` AS dc
    ON dc.`SUBJECT_ID` = cso.`SUBJECT_ID`

  -- left join to se_person by MIT_ID where instructor MIT id is recorded in cso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID
  LEFT JOIN `se_person` AS sp
    ON sp.`MIT_ID` = cso.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`
subject_instructor_dedup.description: For each subject, produce one row per distinct trimmed instructor name (deduplicated) derived from exploded instructor rows. This prepares distinct instructor counts and longest-name length calculations per subject.
counter_examples: For subjects offered in the summer term, list the subject titles, number of instructors, and the length of the longest instructor name.

sis_subject_catalog_rows.name: sis_subject_catalog_rows
sis_subject_catalog_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  sc.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  sc.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  cd.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING AS IS_DEGREE_GRANTING
FROM subject_offered AS so
-- Join to course_catalog_subject_offered to get canonical subject_code/number when available
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered AS sc
  ON sc.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND sc.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
-- Fall back to sis_subject_code / sis_course_description for department/name/degree flag as needed
LEFT JOIN sis_subject_code AS ccode
  ON ccode.COURSE_NUMBER = so.COURSE_NUMBER
  AND ccode.SUBJECT_CODE = sc.SUBJECT_CODE OR (sc.SUBJECT_CODE IS NULL AND ccode.SUBJECT_CODE = so.SUBJECT_ID)
LEFT JOIN sis_course_description AS cd
  ON cd.COURSE = CONCAT(IFNULL(so.SUBJECT_ID,''),' ',IFNULL(so.COURSE_NUMBER,'')) 
  OR cd.DEPARTMENT = so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE
LEFT JOIN sis_course_description AS sd
  ON sd.COURSE = cd.COURSE
sis_subject_catalog_rows.description: Select rows from the SIS subject/course catalog that represent courses offered, keeping canonical course identifiers and the department/school name and degree-granting flag. This isolates the SIS catalog cohort for downstream processing.

departments_core.name: departments_core
departments_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_ID` AS `ORG_ID`,
  `fac_organization`.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  CASE
    WHEN `sis_admin_department`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER` IS NULL OR TRIM(`sis_admin_department`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER`) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN `sis_admin_department`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE` IS NULL OR TRIM(`sis_admin_department`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE`) = '' THEN TRIM(`sis_admin_department`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER`)
    ELSE CONCAT(TRIM(`sis_admin_department`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE`), '-', TRIM(`sis_admin_department`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER`))
  END AS `PHONE`
FROM `fac_organization`
LEFT JOIN `sis_admin_department`
  ON `fac_organization`.`D_CODE` = `sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE`
departments_core.description: Canonical list of departments with their primary identifying key, department name, and phone number (one row per department). Normalizes NULL/empty phone to NULL.

sis_students_core.name: sis_students_core
sis_students_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- required: mit_student_directory.kerberos -> alias kerberos
  `mit_student_directory`.`FULL_NAME` AS `kerberos`,
  -- required: mit_student_directory.display_name -> alias display_name
  COALESCE(`mit_student_directory`.`FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE`, '') AS `display_name`,
  -- required: mit_student_directory.deptid -> alias deptid
  `mit_student_directory`.`DEPARTMENT` AS `deptid`
FROM `mit_student_directory`
sis_students_core.description: Canonical set of students from the Student Information System with their unique student identifier, full name (coalesced to empty string when NULL), and the department identifier they are assigned to.

department_student_counts_and_max_name_l.name: department_student_counts_and_max_name_len
department_student_counts_and_max_name_l.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- deptid: use DEPARTMENT (key) from mit_student_directory
  `mit_student_directory`.`DEPARTMENT` AS deptid,
  -- kerberos: use EMAIL_ADDRESS from mit_student_directory (preserving stored value)
  `mit_student_directory`.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` AS kerberos,
  -- display_name: use FULL_NAME (treat NULL as empty string) from mit_student_directory
  -- but aggregated per department: max length in characters of FULL_NAME (with NULL->'')
  -- Since requirement is to output the display_name column, we provide the MAX length as a string here.
  CAST(MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(COALESCE(`mit_student_directory`.`FULL_NAME`, '')) ) AS CHAR) AS display_name
FROM
  `mit_student_directory`
GROUP BY
  `mit_student_directory`.`DEPARTMENT`
department_student_counts_and_max_name_l.description: For each department (by dept id), compute the distinct student count and the maximum length in characters of students' full names. Treat NULL full names as empty strings.

departments_with_student_metrics.name: departments_with_student_metrics
departments_with_student_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION AS ORG_ID,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AS PHONE,
  msd.DEPARTMENT AS deptid,
  msd.EMAIL_ADDRESS AS kerberos,
  msd.FULL_NAME AS display_name
FROM fac_organization AS fo
LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory AS msd
  ON fo.ORGANIZATION = msd.DEPARTMENT
departments_with_student_metrics.description: Denormalized join of departments to their student aggregates (counts and longest full-name length), one row per department. Keeps departments with zero students (left join).
